# CAMO Compliance Monitoring Manager

**Join 2Excel as our CAMO Compliance Monitoring Manager**

**Reporting to:** Accountable Manager  
**Location:** Doncaster – role requires regular travel to the various 2Excel sites across the UK, hybrid working considered.  
**Type:** Full-time  
**Salary:** Competitive DOE  
**Start Date:** ASAP

**About us**

2Excel Aviation Ltd, part of the 2Excel Group, is an innovative aerospace and aviation services company operating across defence, security, critical national infrastructure, charter, engineering and disaster response. We save lives, clean seas, save trees and support Nationally-important services.  With specialist teams and unrivalled aerospace approvals, we design, build, test and operate aircraft to deliver mission-critical services and data-driven insights. Our success is built on the talent and experience of our exceptional people.

**Why This Role Matters**

At 2Excel, excellent compliance and safety are at the heart of everything we do.  As our CAMO Compliance Monitoring Manager, you won’t just tick boxes, you’ll shape the integrity of our operations, influence Company culture and ensure we demonstrate the highest standards in aviation.

As a Nominated Person, reporting directly to the Accountable Manager and working closely with our AOC Compliance Monitoring Manager, you will be responsible for continuously reviewing and ensuring compliance in line with regulatory requirements and Company procedures for multiple aircraft types across its Continuing Airworthiness Management Organisation (CAMO).

This is your chance to lead from the front, drive continuous improvement, and make a real impact across the business.

**What You’ll Be Doing**

The CAMO CMM acts as the specialist compliance lead for continuing airworthiness oversight.  You will improve, maintain and control a robust compliance monitoring framework, ensuring that CAMO audits, contracted activity oversight, corrective action management, regulatory change impacts and compliance performance are effectively planned, monitored, escalated and reported.

You will identify non-compliances and consequential risks, driving corrective and preventative actions and ensuring our teams are always audit-ready.

You will liaise directly with Regulators and the Company senior leadership, providing clear insights and recommendations.

You’ll act as a deputy for the AOC CMM.

**About you**

You’re likely to have spent much of your career to date within the aviation sector and although you may not always have worked in compliance monitoring, you’ll have proven significant experience of it and be able to effectively develop, run and use a Compliance Management System.  You’ll have practical experience of continuous airworthiness management, aircraft maintenance oversight, CAMO processes or surveillance of such activities.  Candidates who also have experience of AOC and ATO Operators and a deep understanding of ICAO Annex 19 will be at a significant advantage.

You’ll have practical experience of human factors, aviation safety and compliance management systems, standards and practices. You’ll be familiar with audit planning and conducting root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies.  You’ll also have a proactive mindset with a passion for continuous improvement.

This operationally independent role is a CAA Nominated Postholder position.  Therefore, you’ll probably already have experience of working at that level, or you’ve been deputising and you’re ready to take the next step. In order to fulfil this requirement, you’ll have at least 5 years’ relevant work experience with a minimum of 2 years in aeronautical industry roles and/or a relevant engineering degree or maintenance technician qualification acceptable to the CAA. You’ll swiftly be able to demonstrate detailed knowledge of our exposition and operational manuals and understanding of maintenance methods and operational procedures.

You will be a strong communicator, with the confidence to engage, persuade and influence at all levels of our aviation organisation.  You will have excellent organisation skills, with the ability to prioritise your own workload, working under your own initiative and with little guidance.

In addition, applicants must be able to demonstrate the Right to Work in the UK, hold a valid UK Driving Licence due to the travel requirements and obtain a UK Security Clearance (SC).

**What You’ll Get**

* Direct access to the Accountable Manager and senior leadership.
* Opportunities to shape policy and drive innovation.
* A supportive team environment that values your expertise.
* Competitive salary and benefits package which includes but not limited to 25 days of annual leave from day one which increases with length of service, flexible working arrangements, company pension, Group Life Insurance and private medical cover.

**Ready to Elevate Aviation Standards?**

If you’re passionate about compliance, thrive on responsibility and want to be part of a company that values excellence and progress—apply now and help us soar even higher.

To apply, please upload an up to date CV. We would also like you to include a covering letter, telling us how you meet the requirements of the role.

Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Chicago, we are a technology solutions consultancy that partners with organisations from early-stage startups to the world's largest companies. You’ve shown long-term repeated success on a variety of projects, typically over the course of 10+ years. * Built and shipped production-grade platforms: the reusable foundations, tools, infrastructure, and workflows that help other teams shift faster and more reliably
* Taken AI and agentic systems from prototype to production, with a strong understanding of infrastructure, authentication, and observability
* Delivered on  high-stakes consulting engagements across multiple language paradigms, stacks, ecosystems, and client industries

* A track record of understanding, assessing, and embracing new tooling and trends within the software industry
* Built or integrated AI/ML features into products and systems, including recommendation engines, NLP, computer vision, predictive analytics, RAG pipelines, and agents
* Successfully led modernisation and replatforming efforts to align legacy systems with short and long-term business needs
* Led and delivered solutions to architecture-level problems including scalability, security, reliability, performance, maintainability, and observability
* Facilitated alignment across technical and non-technical stakeholders to move initiatives forward through ambiguity and complexity
* Provided mentorship and team support at scale, while sharing knowledge and improving team practices
* Collaboratively led stakeholders to balance technical considerations with product and user needs
* Actively sought out and effectively given feedback

## **What You’ll Do At 8th Light**

As a go-to technologist and strategist within 8th Light, you’ll work with a variety of clients, typically one to two in a year, while continuing to deepen your and our collective domain expertise over the course of your career with us. You’ll be responsible for:

* Rapidly building trust with clients, demonstrating technical expertise and understanding of their domain and objectives
* Driving platform engineering work at the client level, connecting long-term technical vision to what ships
* Leading platform strategy and delivery across diverse platform types, connecting long-term vision to what ships
* Working pragmatically to balance technology choices while delivering high-quality work within deadlines
* Advising clients on architecture, scalability and platform evolution, connecting technical decisions to product and business outcomes
* Collaborating on systems that involve the full ML lifecycle from data ingestion and preprocessing, to model deployment, integration, and performance monitoring
* Driving innovation by proactively surfacing new technical approaches and product solutions
* Leading or initiating formal feedback conversations with teams and clients via retrospectives
* Clearly articulating and documenting outcomes and driving forward action items
* Contributing to the health of your team and 8th Light’s culture by modeling our Values
* Designing and managing high-level technical roadmaps for large engagements
* Building your network and maintaining relationships with clients and other industry leaders within your domain
* Coaching client engineering teams, transferring knowledge and leveling up practices
* Influencing client CTOs and executive decisions. Planning and execute technical work that involves stakeholders outside of project boundaries such as across a client's technical organization
* Partner with account teams on planning, opportunity identification, stakeholder relationships, and pre-sales scope shaping
* Facilitating retrospectives, strategy sessions, and technical deep-dives to improve team and project outcomes
* Identifying, mitigating, and resolving blockers to team progress
* Contributing to 8th Light by serving as a mentor, leading or designing workshops internally or for clients, representing 8th Light in the tech community, or supporting our hiring processes
* Demonstrating leadership in scalable system design, modular architecture, and platform- or product-oriented development
* Bringing depth in testing strategies, observability, fault tolerance, and secure engineering practices
* Applying architectural patterns to evaluate tradeoffs and drive clear, documented design rationale

## **Strongly Preferred Skills**

We work across many areas, and encourage anyone with the experience listed above to apply. We would particularly like to encourage applicants with experience in the following areas:

* Platform engineering: building reusable software foundations, internal developer platforms, and infrastructure that other teams build on
* Data Engineering: including platforms like Databricks for data processing and analytics
* Delivering production agentic systems, including RAG pipelines, vector search, and agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, AutoGen, and n8n
* DevSecOps & DevOps
* MLOps
* Infrastructure as Code

Building a truly diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace is an ongoing journey, and we’re excited to keep learning and growing together. We have a proud tradition of hiring talented colleagues with real-world career experiences.

At 8th Light, we believe our people are our greatest asset. Their growth, well-being, and success shape our future.

* Our wellness package is designed with the Whole YOU in mind and includes:
* A robust L&D programme featuring unlimited access to thousands of books, courses, and expert-led training on the O'Reilly learning platform.
* Annual financial stipend and time allotment for learning & development
* Coworking support for our global team
* 12 weeks of new parent leave available for eligible employees

See our full list of Benefits.

At 8th Light, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that is transparent, fair, and helps us attract and retain top talent in alignment with our company’s strategic growth goals and clients’ needs.

We benchmark our salaries using Geographic Structures to establish competitive pay ranges within the regions where 8th Lights live. Our pay ranges for our Principal Engineer position within London is: £92,818-£116,122 GBP

Reach out to recruiting@8thlight.com for more relevant information pertaining to your local market.

## **8th Light Hubs and Geographies**

8th Light's culture is rooted in strong connections that extend across our teams, regions, and beyond client work. We are a distributed team across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with hubs in Chicago, London, Los Angeles, New York, and Seattle.

* **London Co-working:** Employees working from our London hub follow a hybrid model, which includes a minimum of one day per week in our Waterloo Office. **Scottish Friendly Wellbeing Service**

Action for Children’s Scottish Friendly Wellbeing Service started in June 2023 and have secured funding until June 2027. The aim of the service is to improve the mental health and wellbeing of vulnerable school pupils in Glasgow and aimed at schools with the highest levels of need, as evidenced through Scottish Government Table of SIMD.

The Family Support Practitioner will support with the growing element of the service which is direct support for families and young people in their homes and local communities. The service has a more focussed, young person led, approach to mental health and emotional wellbeing using an early intervention approach to deliver sustainable improvements.  The Family Support Practitioner will be based primarily in the school helping to identify needs earlier and take appropriate action if needed to further mental health and wellbeing services.

Interventions that will be provided by the Family Support practitioner will include:

**Direct Support**

The impact of direct support provided to young people who require this higher-tier intervention will be measured using the “My Mind Star” Outcomes Star tool, which assesses emotional wellbeing. This can also include direct work with families in the home or community as well being 1:1 with young people within the school.

**Bouncing Back**

Bouncing Back is an early resilience programme which is a lower-level intervention than Blues. It gives large groups of children and young people useful and evidenced based tools to support their wellbeing. This process also supports us to identify young people who need a higher-tier intervention, such as Blues or direct support.

**Blues**

The Blues Programme is an internationally acclaimed wellbeing programme for young people aged 13-19. Over six weeks, it teaches emotional resilience and reduces low mood and anxious thoughts.

Job ID: 10468018 | Amazon Data Services UK Limited - E17

## Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.  
  
You will collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. At AWS you will experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
Colo Physical Security Architects at AWS work with our Colocation Vendor partners to design safe, secure, resilient, cost-effective Data Center (DC) facilities. As a Colo Physical Security Architect, you will lead security designs for Colocation DCs throughout our Europe, Middle East and Africa Region and impact AWS global colo data center security standards. You will be part of a highly creative and efficient design team comprised of Architects, Engineers, and Designers tasked with solving problems and challenging the status quo. As a subject matter expert, you will provide technical guidance, have a direct impact on the design of Colo data center facilities, solve large-scale implementation issues, and be responsible for developing and communicating security design requirements to internal and external project partners.  
  
As a Colo Physical Security Architect, you will work directly with other AWS Security Teams, AWS Management, and Colo Vendor partners to collaborate in the real-world application of Physical Security throughout AWS. ## Overview

We are keen to hear from candidates with location preferences across any of our UK network of offices, working alongside our growing team of social and behavioural researchers based in Birmingham, Bristol, Epsom, London (Victoria) and Manchester, or our other hubs in Belfast, Cambridge, Edinburgh or York.

You’ll combine a strong understanding of evaluation theory with excellent project management and client engagement skills. We are particularly interested in candidates who can bring experience in **evaluation theory, benefits management, data analysis, digital tools and AI-enabled approaches** to evaluation. You will lead and support the delivery of mixed-methods evaluation projects, advise clients on proportionate and robust methodological approaches, and contribute to the continued growth of AtkinsRéalis’ research and evaluation offer.

## Your role

We are looking for Senior or Principal level Evaluation and Social Research Consultant to join our ambitious, friendly and growing team that combines specialists in social research, behavioural science and evaluation, delivering projects for a range of local and national transport bodies. Evaluation and social research are vital for transport policy and planning. They provide essential evidence to design successful policies, programmes and interventions, and to understand the impacts of transport investments on people, places and economies.

* Work on varied and meaningful evaluation projects across the UK.
* Collaborate with specialists across multiple disciplines and sectors.
* Help grow an important area of transport planning, policy and consultancy work.

* Develop your technical, commercial and leadership skills.

You should be flexible, self‐motivated, and able to demonstrate relevant knowledge and technical experience commensurate with your level of experience. We are particularly interested in applications from people who have worked in market research, evaluation, or economics who a passion for robust evidence and insight. Knowledge of the transport sector is not essential, but an interest and willingness to learn is desirable.

**Essential experience**

* Experience of designing and delivering evaluations of policies, programmes or projects, ideally in transport, infrastructure, public policy, local government, social value, regeneration or related sectors.

* Experience of leading and contributing to proposals, bids or business development activity.
* Collaborative working style: strong communication, collaboration and interpersonal skills, with a commitment to quality, inclusion, ethical research practice and continuous improvement.

**Desirable experience**

* A postgraduate qualification or demonstrable professional development in evaluation, social research, economics, data analysis or a related discipline, with good knowledge of evaluation theory and practice, such as theory-based evaluation, process evaluation, impact evaluation, mixed-methods approaches, quasi-experimental approaches, realist evaluation, contribution analysis or value-for-money evaluation.

* Digital and AI: an interest and curiosity in how digital tools and AI-enabled tools can improve the efficiency, quality and value of evaluation and benefits management.

You will prepare and develop artwork for Make-Ready and Avant Arte’s silkscreen and digital print editions. You will be expected to manage your priorities and work with the Senior Artworker and Master Printer on your technical development. You will take ownership of assigned tasks, building independence as your skills develop and recognising when to ask for guidance.

**We think the ideal candidate is:**

* **Accountable and organised.** You take responsibility for your work, check the details and meet agreed deadlines. When something may affect delivery, you raise it early and help find a solution.
* **Curious and practical.** You enjoy understanding how an image becomes a physical print, ask thoughtful questions and respond constructively to feedback.
* **Reliable and collaborative.** You are punctual, communicate clearly and work well in a busy studio, supporting the successful delivery of the whole project.

**Skills and experience:**

* Confident using Adobe Photoshop, with experience preparing and adjusting image files. Familiarity with Adobe Illustrator and InDesign is desirable.
* A good eye for colour and detail, with an understanding of resolution, image dimensions, layers and colour profiles. Able to keep files organised and manage revisions accurately.
* Experience in artworking, pre-press, digital print or a related field. Silkscreen colour separation, RIP software and large-format inkjet experience are desirable but not 100% necessary; highly specialist processes can be developed through training with Senior Artworker and Master Printer.

**Key roles & responsibilities:**

**Artworking and colour separation**

Prepare artwork for silkscreen and digital editions under Senior Artworker and Master Printer’s direction, including image adjustments, sizing, colour separations. Follow agreed specifications and prepare clearly labelled files for proofing and production.

Prepare artwork for silkscreen and digital editions, including image adjustments, sizing, colour separations and other artworking tasks. Follow agreed specifications and prepare clearly labelled files for proofing and production. Seek guidance from the Senior Artworker and Master Printer where necessary.

**Proof development**

Work with the printmakers to develop proofs, explore practical options and respond to feedback, both internal and from the artist. Make controlled adjustments to colour, tone and separations, recording changes so the team can compare versions and reproduce agreed results.

**Film positives and digital output**

Prepare and output film positives, digital samples and assigned digital prints using the studio’s equipment and approved workflows. Check scale, quality and registration before release, and flag and rectify inconsistencies promptly.

**File checks and quality control**

Check supplied files against project requirements, including dimensions, resolution and suitability for the intended process. Complete agreed checks at key stages, raise missing information or technical concerns with the Senior Artworker, and ensure the correct approved version is used for production.

**Project information and communication**

Keep job sheets, artwork files and revision records accurate and up to date. Share clear information with the printmakers and relevant project colleagues so that specifications, changes and next steps are understood. Lead kick offs for assigned projects.

**Planning and delivery**

Work to the priorities and timelines agreed in the schedule. Send updates of progress, workload and any risks to delivery. Being fully accountable for completing assigned work and seeking guidance when a decision falls outside your experience or agreed scope.

**Print knowledge and efficient working**

Develop your understanding of silkscreen and fine art digital printing, materials and studio capabilities. Follow established processes and suggest practical improvements that reduce errors and rework.

**Equipment and studio contribution**

Carry out routine checks, cleaning and maintenance of artworking and digital output equipment. Report faults promptly, maintain an organised workspace and support wider studio tasks when required. Finally, be constantly curious about the process and always seek to push what is possible within a day, not just hit existing rate limits.

Contribute to an open, respectful and collaborative studio. Cherish feedback, share useful learning and approach challenges with honesty and initiative through professional channels. Understand how your work and presence contributes to delivering editions on time and on budget.

Purpose of Role
The Principal Data Platform Architect is responsible for defining and maintaining the strategic direction of the enterprise data platform, ensuring it provides scalable, governed and well-adopted capabilities for data ingestion, creation, movement, transformation, governance and monitoring.

The role will establish the vision, roadmap, architectural principles and delivery priorities for the platform, working closely with the Principal Platform Architect, Principal Solutions Architect and Principal Data Architect to ensure that data platform strategy and architecture form part of a coherent, joined-up enterprise architecture. This collaboration is critical to ensuring clear architectural boundaries and accountabilities, effective management of cross-domain dependencies, and alignment between data, platform, solution and wider technology strategies.

The role will also work closely with Data Governance, engineering teams, business stakeholders and external partners to ensure the data platform evolves in line with the firm's strategic priorities and business needs.

The role reports to the Head of Data Services.
Responsibilities
Act as strategic product owner for the enterprise data platform and associated tooling, translating business, governance and engineering needs into a clear set of platform capabilities, priorities and roadmaps.
Develop and maintain the data platform architecture strategy, including current, future and transition states, ensuring it remains aligned with the firm's data and technology strategies and continues to be fit for purpose.
Define and maintain the technical and design principles for the data platform, ensuring they are widely understood and consistently adopted.
Work closely with the Principal Platform Architect, Principal Solutions Architect and Principal Data Architect to align architecture strategies, principles and roadmaps, manage cross-domain dependencies and resolve areas of overlap or architectural tension.
Work collaboratively with Data Governance and senior stakeholders and external partners to ensure the platform supports the firm's data architecture, business needs, governance requirements and relevant standards.
Prioritise, sponsor and drive strategic data platform initiatives, ensuring expected outcomes, benefits, risks and dependencies are clearly understood and providing leadership to shape initiatives where required.
Represent the data platform in relevant governance and architecture forums, including the Data Strategy Management Group and Design Authority, ensuring decisions align with agreed principles, standards, risk appetite and long-term strategy.
Work closely with engineering, delivery and platform teams to support good engineering practice, maintain clear roadmaps and dependencies, and ensure appropriate documentation and training are in place.
Maintain strong technical and industry knowledge, using external insight, peer networks and technology partners to inform the ongoing evolution of the data platform.
Facilitate resolution of complex platform issues and dependencies, bringing together internal teams, architects and external vendors as required to achieve effective outcomes.
What does success look like:
A clear future roadmap for the data platform is agreed and well understood across the firm.
Concrete steps have been taken to simplify and unify how the data platform is used.
Platform principles, standards and priorities are clear and consistently applied.
Strong alignment is established with the Principal Data, Platform and Solutions Architects on cross-domain direction and dependencies.
Your knowledge and experience:
Strong experience shaping enterprise data platform strategy.
Expertise in data architecture, platform design/product management.
Strong understanding of data engineering concepts
Good knowledge of data governance, controls and architectural standards.
Experience with cloud data platforms and technologies, including Snowflake.
Strong understanding of data quality, observability, security and risk management.
Good awareness of the wider technology landscape and vendors.
Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving and commercial judgement.
Confident leadership and influencing skills.
Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building ability.
Clear, engaging communication and storytelling skills.
Sound decision-making and prioritisation.
A strong product ownership mindset.
Good understanding of governance and assurance.
Curiosity, continuous learning and strong external awareness.

We’re looking for someone who is excited by the challenge of shaping the foundations of data is stored, moved, transformed and used across a complex organisation. You’ll bring strong experience of modern data platforms and architecture, but just as importantly, you’ll be able to turn that expertise into a clear, practical vision that others can understand and support. You’ll be comfortable thinking strategically while staying close enough to the detail to make sound decisions on platform design.

We’d particularly value someone who is curious, commercially aware and interested in how the data technology landscape is evolving, with a genuine desire to build a platform that is simpler, more consistent and easier for teams across the firm to use.

# FP&A Analyst

Newcastle

### **About Behavox**

Behavox is a cloud-native AI company providing an integrated controls platform for global banks, asset managers, hedge funds, private equity firms, insurance businesses, and commodity firms. The platform unifies communications and trade surveillance, compliant archiving, policy management as well as front-office analytics on a single, AI-native technology stack, delivered as a globally scalable SaaS-based cloud service.

At Behavox, our engineering culture is built around speed, experimentation, and technical excellence, following agile principles and rapid iteration. We constantly test and adopt the latest cloud technologies and AI tooling, optimising for fast feedback loops and execution. We look for people who can move fast, challenge conventional wisdom, and who want to work at the frontier of modern AI, SaaS platforms, and distributed systems.

Behavox is a high-performance organisation with a strong bias toward delivery, ownership, and responsibility. We commit, and we execute. We are building systems that are complex, mission-critical, and global in scale; systems that many consider too large or too difficult. To do that, we seek the smartest, most technically capable engineers and technologists who take end-to-end responsibility and want to win by building what others cannot.

Founded in 2014 and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Behavox is headquartered in London, with offices worldwide, including New York City, Montreal, Seattle, Singapore, and Tokyo.

### **About the Role**

The Senior FP&A Analyst owns Behavox's core financial model — its architecture, the accounting beneath it, and the forecasts and analysis the company plans and decides by. The role exists to change decisions, not report them: it turns the numbers into the choices leadership actually faces. It reads and integrates budgets into the model, but does not run the budgeting cycle.

The same analyst builds the valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma models behind every acquisition — evaluating targets, running diligence, and folding closed deals into a single consolidated view. This work is periodic and must be carried alone when it arrives; the steady state is the operating model and SaaS forecasting.

This is a high-autonomy role that works without a detailed brief and sets the modeling standard others build on. It is accountable for the accuracy and integrity of the numbers, and for turning them into recommendations sharp enough to act on — the downside case included, not just the point estimate — for senior leadership, the board, and investors. It pressure-tests the assumptions behind every result, works fluently with modern tooling and AI, and compounds that edge by learning relentlessly. Its influence comes from the rigor and reach of the analysis, not from authority: it owns the model and the truth it tells, not the decisions made from it.

### **What You'll Bring**

1. **Financial Model & Accounting Foundations** — Knows how an integrated three-statement and operating model fits together, and the accounting that holds it up — SaaS revenue recognition and cost treatment included. Understands exactly how the company's budgets are built, and folds them into the model.
2. **Forecasting & SaaS Unit Economics** — Knows both bottom-up short-term forecasting and driver-based long-term modeling, and the SaaS metrics that actually reveal performance. Knows what moves each one and which lever changes it — not just how to report it.
3. **Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration** — Knows how to value an acquisition and how to fold it into one consolidated model: purchase accounting, combined-entity projections, and the mechanics that make or break the integration.
4. **Business & Commercial Acumen** — Knows in depth how the business and every function make money — the revenue drivers, the cost structure, the operating levers — and spots a number that doesn't add up on sight.
5. **Financial Systems & AI Tooling** — Commands Google Sheets and Excel, and tracks the AI and automation landscape closely enough to know where it is trustworthy and where it isn't.

### **What You'll Do**

1. **Financial Model Ownership** — Builds and maintains the core three-statement and operating model with scenario and sensitivity layers, and keeps it accurate, clean, and easy to maintain. Integrates budgets without owning the cycle, and owns the accuracy of every output and the integrity of every assumption.
2. **Acquisition Modeling & Integration** — Builds the valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma combined-entity models behind acquisition evaluation and due diligence, and folds closed deals into a single consolidated view.
3. **Business-Review Reporting** — Drives much of the substance of the monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews — with the broader FP&A team — for senior management, the board, and investors, turning the model into a narrative that explains what moved the results and what it means for the business.
4. **Metrics Analysis & Business Partnering** — Diagnoses why the metrics are moving and which lever changes them, pressure-tests the assumptions behind every result, and hands the decision-maker a recommendation they can act on.
5. **AI-Enabled Productivity** — Uses AI and spreadsheet automation to compress cycle time and harden data validation — automating the recurring work while keeping judgment on what stays manual.

### **What We Offer**

* The opportunity to work on a global, mission-critical AI platform alongside the best engineers and technologists across multiple geographies.
* A role with real ownership and impact, building complex systems at scale in an environment that values speed, experimentation, and technical excellence.
* A highly attractive benefits package, including competitive cash compensation, and an equity award aligned with long-term value creation.
* A generous time-off policy of 30 days annually, plus public holidays and sick leave, recognizing the importance of sustained high performance.

### **About Our Process**

We take Talent very seriously and we are building a community of extraordinary individuals working together in very high performing teams. We also know that the best Talent always has options so we believe that the process has to be a two way assessment - the company AND the candidate assessing the business needs alignment, the career next step alignment, and the cultural alignment.   
  
During the process we will begin by exploring the core factors regarding salary and location along with core experience and skills and values alignment. We will then deep dive explore the critical technical competencies we have identified for the role, and then we will deep dive in behavioral competencies.  
  
The most aligned candidate will then be asked to do a practical work task simulation activity so we can make sure that you will enjoy the kind of work the role requires, and this task will typically be presented and discussed with a group of colleagues and managers. Finally we will ask you to meet with a number of our senior leaders to make sure that you are making the most informed call possible.

### **Please note that:**

* We want to get to know you and have a genuine conversation, so the use of AI tools or assistance during live interviews is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification from the process
* Interviews may be recorded for internal review purposes to ensure fairness and enable collaborative hiring discussions within the team.

# Police Officer - Inner London

## Job Introduction

**Now Recruiting Police Officers in Central London**

Be part of something new – Join us as we launch the Police Constable Entry Programme  
  
*"BTP truly is a unique police* *force* *with a real family* *feel**. We care deeply about what we do; serving the public and* *supporting* *our people. Our work matters.* *If you want to make a positive difference to the millions of people who use the network every day, BTP is the place for you**."* **– Chris Casey, Divisional Commander, London and South East England**

We are recruiting Police Officers within**Inner London**.  
Locations include, but are not limited to, stations such as Kings Cross, Euston, Wembley, Croydon, Clapham Junction, West Ham, Waterloo and Stratford.

**Please note:** You cannot choose a specific Inner London posting location. However, we will take your home location into account wherever operationally possible when allocating postings.

### Could this be the role for you?

As a Police Officer with British Transport Police, you'll play a vital role in keeping millions of passengers, railway staff and members of the public safe every day. Working across one of the busiest transport networks in the world, you'll face unique challenges, develop valuable skills and make a real difference to people's lives.

No two days are the same. One moment, you could be supporting a vulnerable person in crisis. The next, you might be responding to an emergency, investigating crime, safeguarding a child, disrupting criminal activity or reassuring someone during one of the most difficult moments of their life.

This is a career where your actions matter. Every interaction provides an opportunity to protect, support and positively impact the communities we serve.

You'll never face these challenges alone. From your first day of training, you'll be supported by experienced colleagues, supervisors and mentors who are committed to helping you develop, succeed and build a rewarding career.

We offer one of the most competitive starting salary packages for Police Constables in England and Wales, alongside excellent benefits, structured career development and opportunities to specialise throughout your policing career.  
  
**What you'll get in return**

A successful policing career is about more than salary alone. At British Transport Police, you'll benefit from competitive pay, industry-leading travel benefits, strong family-friendly policies, comprehensive wellbeing support and ongoing opportunities to develop both professionally and personally.

* **Starting salary:** £33,609, rising year on year to £52,014 after five years
* **London allowances:** £9,044.75 (£5,783.75 London Allowance plus £3,261 London Weighting) from day one of training
* Oyster card for personal and professional use
* 25 days annual leave, increasing with service
* A highly competitive Career Average Revalued Earnings (CARE) pension scheme
* Voucher and incentive schemes, including cycle-to-work and a wide range of retail discounts
* Continued investment in learning, supported by dedicated in-house talent and development teams
* Clear promotion and career development opportunities across a range of policing specialisms
* Specialist support from Occupational Health and wellbeing services
* Free eyesight tests
* Eligibility for the Blue Light Card
* Membership of the Police Federation from day one
* Strong support for work-life balance, including 26 weeks of fully paid maternity leave, alongside paternity leave, carers' leave, adoption leave and special leave provisions

### What we're looking for

You do not need previous policing experience to join us. We welcome applications from people from all backgrounds, experiences and stages of life.

Whether you're changing careers, leaving education, returning to work or looking for a fresh challenge, we'll provide the training, support and development you need to succeed. There is no single background that makes a great police officer. Some of our officers join directly from education, while others bring valuable experience from careers in healthcare, customer service, retail, hospitality, transportation, the military and many other professions.

What matters most is your integrity, commitment to helping others and willingness to learn. If you care about people, enjoy working as part of a team and want to make a difference, we'd love to hear from you. While every day brings different challenges, successful officers are often people who communicate effectively, remain calm under pressure and can build positive relationships with people from all walks of life.

**Key qualities include:**

* Strong communication skills
* Sound judgement and problem-solving ability
* Empathy and emotional resilience
* The ability to build trust and remain calm under pressure

**Police Constable Entry Programme (PCEP)**

Successful candidates will join the Police Constable Entry Programme (PCEP), British Transport Police's two-year entry route for new police officers.

You do not need a degree to apply and you will not be required to complete a degree as part of the programme.

PCEP combines classroom learning, remote learning, scenario-based training and practical operational experience to equip you with the knowledge, skills and behaviours needed for frontline policing.

During training, you'll learn how to:

* Use policing powers lawfully and effectively
* Prevent and investigate crime
* Protect vulnerable people
* Respond to incidents and emergencies
* Support victims and witnesses
* Keep passengers, railway staff and local communities safe

As your career develops, you'll have opportunities to specialise in areas such as CID, Counter Terrorism and County Lines. Whether you aspire to become a detective, join a specialist unit, develop as a leader or continue building expertise in frontline policing, we'll support your ambitions every step of the way.

**Entry Requirements**

To be eligible to apply for the Police Constable Entry Programme (PCEP), you must have:

* Level 2 qualifications in English Language and Maths (GCSE Grade C/4 or above, or an accepted equivalent qualification), or be willing to undertake BTP's Level 2 English and Maths assessment if you do not currently hold these qualifications; and
* Either:
  + Hold a Level 3 or above, or
  + Have relevant work experience demonstrating an equivalent level of knowledge, responsibility and professional capability.

If you do not currently hold a Level 2 qualification in English and/or Maths, British Transport Police can provide an assessment to enable you to demonstrate the required Level 2 standard as part of the recruitment process.

Examples of Level 3 qualifications include:

* Two A-levels at grade E or above (or equivalent, such as a BTEC Level 3, Level 3 T Levels or International Baccalaureate).
* BTEC National Diploma
* NVQ Level 3
* Access to Higher Education Diploma
* Other recognised Level 3 qualifications
* Policing experience: at least 12 months' relevant experience, including service as a Special Constable (independent patrol status), PCSO and staff.

We recognise that qualifications are only one measure of potential. If you do not hold a Level 3 qualification, we may consider relevant work experience as an alternative route into policing.

Relevant work experience (24 months service) in one of the following areas:

* Armed Forces / Military service
* Emergency services (e.g. ambulance, fire)
* Revenue Protection Officer / Revenue Inspector
* Railway Enforcement Officer
* Rail Incident Response or Service Delivery Management roles

Candidates will be required to provide evidence of their qualifications and/or experience during the recruitment process.  
  
**You will not be eligible to apply if:**

* You do not hold Level 2 English Language and Maths qualifications (GCSE Grade C/4 or above, or an accepted equivalent qualification).
* You cannot demonstrate either a Level 3 qualification or relevant work experience equivalent to Level 3.
* You have been unsuccessful following your application, testing or interview for Police Officer, Special Constable or PCSO and have not yet completed the three-month reapplication period.
* You have been declined/refused vetting in the last two years by BTP or any other police force, NCA, CNC or MOD.
* You have ever received a custodial sentence, including suspended sentences.
* You have previously been dismissed from another police force or are subject to a live misconduct investigation.
* You are bankrupt, have a County Court Judgment, or an unmanaged Individual Voluntary Arrangement.
* You have tattoos deemed offensive (face and neck tattoos are considered on a case-by-case basis).
* You do not have permanent right to live and work in the UK.
* You have not resided continuously in the UK for the past three years.

### Want to apply?

Applications are completed online.

As part of the process, you will be required to complete a Situational Judgement Test & also an Ethic Situational Judgement Test. If you do not pass the SJT assessments, your application will not progress at this time, though you may reapply once the reapplication period allows.

You are encouraged, though not required, to attend a question-and-answer session to learn more about the role, life at BTP and the recruitment process.

Please note: This campaign is for new recruits only. Transferees should apply through a transferee-specific vacancy when available.

Successful applicants will join a conditional offer pool and be considered for opportunities for up to 12 months from the date of their conditional offer.

### Equality, Diversity and Inclusion

We are committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and able to thrive.

We believe our people are strongest when they reflect the diverse communities we serve, and we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and lived experiences.

Whatever your background, identity or experience, you'll be supported throughout the recruitment process and throughout your career with British Transport Police.

Reasonable adjustments are available at every stage of the recruitment process.

### Use of AI in applications

AI can be a useful tool for generating ideas or helping structure written responses, but we want to hear your genuine voice. Personal experiences, authentic motivation and individual insight are what stand out most to us.

**Application deadline: Midnight on Monday 14th December 2026**

Please note that this campaign may close early if a high volume of applications is received.

For support or assistance with your application, contact the Recruitment Team - recruitmentteam@btp.police.uk

**Join British Transport Police and build a career where you'll be supported, valued and empowered to make a meaningful difference every day.**

# Graduate AI and Secure Technologies Engineer (2026 start)

**Cambridge, UK**  
**UK travel and occasional international travel**

### **Introduction**

We’re looking for graduates who are excited by the opportunity to make emerging technologies secure, trustworthy and resilient. You’ll work on real-world engineering challenges across cyber security, artificial intelligence, embedded systems and connected technologies, supporting projects in areas including defence and security, industrial systems and critical national infrastructure.

You’ll need to be curious, willing to learn and comfortable exploring unfamiliar technical problems. In return, we’ll provide the support, mentoring and hands-on experience you need to develop into a confident, well-rounded security engineer working on innovative deep technology.

We’re much more interested in the engineer you can become than the one you are now. We’ll give you the time, support and opportunities to build your security engineering skills and develop the confidence to contribute to challenging client projects. Curiosity, a careful and structured approach to problem solving, and enthusiasm for technology are more important than having experience in every area of cyber security.

## 

### **Overview**

Cambridge Consultants develops deep technology across sensing, communications, embedded systems, artificial intelligence and complex systems. Our Trusted AI and Secure Technologies team helps clients understand, design and demonstrate security and trustworthiness in emerging and connected technologies.

You’ll work as part of multidisciplinary teams alongside engineers and specialists in electronics, firmware, software, RF, AI and data science, and systems engineering. Projects can span the full engineering lifecycle, from early-stage concepts and requirements through to implementation, verification, deployment and in-service support.

Our work includes cyber security, secure-by-design engineering, embedded and connected systems, industrial and critical infrastructure, defence and national security, edge AI, secure connectivity and post-quantum cryptography.

### **Your responsibilities**

You’ll work on real client assignments with support and guidance from experienced engineers. You’ll have opportunities to contribute across different stages of the engineering lifecycle and work alongside specialists from across Cambridge Consultants.

You may contribute to projects at different stages of the engineering lifecycle, from early-stage concept development and requirements through to architecture, implementation, verification, deployment and in-service support.

You’ll also have opportunities to interact directly with clients, including requirements discussions, technical workshops, progress updates and delivery, with support from experienced engineers where appropriate.

### **What you’ll be doing**

* Contributing to threat modelling, attack-surface analysis and security risk assessments.
* Helping to identify security requirements and develop secure-by-design system architectures.
* Supporting vulnerability assessments and security testing, including helping to scope testing activities and track remediation.
* Investigating vulnerabilities and helping teams understand and address security risks.
* Contributing to security cases, assurance activities and technical documentation.
* Analysing systems, software and technical designs to identify potential security weaknesses.
* Developing prototypes, analysis tools or other technical solutions to investigate security problems.
* Working with multidisciplinary teams to understand the interaction between security, functionality, safety and system performance.
* Communicating technical findings clearly to engineers, project teams and customers.

**Domains and project types**

You could work across a range of applications and technologies, including:

* **Critical national infrastructure:** energy, transport, communications and utilities.
* **Industrial systems:** ICS, SCADA, OT and industrial IoT.
* **Defence and national security:** secure systems and technologies supporting demanding operational environments.
* **Emerging technologies:** AI assurance, sensing, secure connectivity and post-quantum cryptography.

### **What you can bring**

**The below is essential**

* An excellent degree or PhD in Computer Science, Cyber Security, Electronic/Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Physics or a related technical discipline.
* 12 months industrial experience, for example through a placement year or relevant postgraduate experience.
* A good understanding of fundamental engineering, computing or security principles.
* Practical experience through university, industrial placement, work experience, research or personal projects in at least one or more relevant areas, such as:

* + cyber/security engineering
  + software or application development
  + embedded systems
  + computer or network systems
  + electronics or hardware security
  + AI or data science
  + systems engineering

* The ability to understand and analyse technical systems and identify risks or weaknesses.
* Some familiarity with security concepts such as authentication, authorisation, cryptography, key management, secure boot, network security and secure development.
* The ability to read and understand code in languages such as C, C++, Python or Java.
* Enthusiasm for learning and developing new technical skills.
* A careful and structured approach to problem solving.
* Clear communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with others.

**The below is advantageous, but isn’t essential**

* Familiarity with threat-modelling approaches such as STRIDE or MITRE ATT&CK.
* Knowledge of secure development practices and frameworks such as OWASP or CWE.
* Experience with embedded platforms, MCUs, RTOS, TPMs or TrustZone.
* Familiarity with industrial protocols and standards such as Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA or IEC 62443.
* Experience using tools such as Burp Suite, Wireshark or firmware-analysis tools.
* An understanding of cloud security.
* Experience considering security alongside safety or other system-level requirements.
* Security research, university projects, technical projects or open-source contributions.
* Industry certifications or formal security training.

Some projects at Cambridge Consultants are subject to security restrictions. This role requires you to obtain a Security Check level security clearance ( https://www.gov.uk/guidance/united-kingdom-security-vetting-applicant ). You must be able to work in the UK without restrictions in accordance with UK National Law and be prepared to successfully undertake an appropriate level of UK National Security Vetting according to UK Government National Security Vetting criteria.

Along with your CV, please describe why you are attracted to this position, what you feel you offer Cambridge Consultants, and any achievements that you are particularly proud of. We are especially interested to hear about any projects you have done, for a hobby, for work or for university.

We welcome applications from individuals who wish to be considered for part-time working or other flexible working arrangements.

Advanced therapies based on modified mRNA and antisense oligonucleotides are transforming the treatment of cancer, neurodegenerative disease and infection, but their full potential will only be realised if they can be designed to be both powerful and safe. This post will develop new experimental systems to understand how these therapeutics activate innate immune pathways, and to use that knowledge to make them "safer by design". The successful candidate will work at the interface of RNA biology, immunology and toxicology, building models that identify when immune activation is harmful, when it can be harnessed for therapeutic benefit, and how these responses can be engineered in the next generation of nucleic acid medicines.

A Research Associate is required to establish new experimental models to understand how nucleic acid therapeutics, including antisense oligonucleotides and modified mRNA therapeutics, activate innate immune signalling pathways in complex models. The post will sit within a new collaborative programme between the laboratories of James Thaventhiran, Marion MacFarlane and Anne Willis at the MRC Toxicology Unit and AstraZeneca R&D, and foster collaboration with Menna Clatworthy, Fotios Sampaziotis and Eoin McKinney at CITIID, University of Cambridge. They will work within an MRC-funded Prosperity Partnership with AstraZeneca, improving cell models, to enable high-throughput quantification of the contribution of immune cells and immune signalling to the oligonucleotide tissue response.

The central aim of the post is to develop robust, mechanistically informative systems that can detect and dissect immune activation by therapeutic nucleic acids. The post-holder will use these models to identify the molecular features and cellular pathways that determine inflammatory, toxic or therapeutically useful responses. They will then test strategies to modify these responses, either to reduce unwanted toxicity or to enhance therapeutic efficacy.  
The project will provide an opportunity to work across cellular immunology, RNA biology, translational toxicology and advanced pre-clinical models. Depending on the direction of the work, this includes reporter cell-model generation, CRISPR or perturbation-based approaches, transcriptomic and proteomic analysis, modified mRNA and ASO delivery systems, murine models, and ex vivo perfused human organ systems.

The post is intended to support the development of an outstanding early-career scientist towards research independence. The successful candidate will be encouraged to generate a coherent body of preliminary data over the first two years in post, with the aim of developing a competitive postdoctoral fellowship application to schemes such as those offered by Wellcome, MRC, Cancer Research UK or equivalent funders.

The post would suit a highly motivated scientist with a strong background in innate immunology, advanced organoid/3D culture models, RNA biology, molecular cell biology, medicines safety, nucleic acid therapeutics or related disciplines. We are particularly interested in candidates who can combine rigorous experimental biology with the intellectual drive to shape a new area of translational research.  
Applicants must hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in a relevant discipline.

You’ll join a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists working on our core automation platform, from first prototypes through to production systems. You’ll design, implement and test firmware that runs on ARM microcontrollers, work directly with hardware on the bench, and help shape technical decisions across firmware, electronics and the wider system.

* Turn system needs into clear firmware requirements and interfaces, working directly with electronics, mechanical, automation and software engineers, plus biologists.
* Make and communicate technical decisions within your area, balancing engineering rigour, maintainability and delivery speed, and support other engineers through design discussions and code reviews.
* Debug complex embedded-system issues using tools such as debug probes, oscilloscopes, multimeters and logic analysers, getting to the root cause of tricky problems.
* Use Linux-based tools and development environments as part of your day-to-day work.
* Support and occasionally develop custom test equipment for internal use, helping the wider team move faster.
* Use higher-level languages such as Python, C# or Java to build supporting tools and simple GUIs for debugging, testing or internal users.

* Turn your hand to electronics design and prototype modification when needed, working with electronics engineers to shape interfaces and resolve cross-discipline issues.
* Develop and optimise hard real-time algorithms for motion control, sensing or safety-critical functions.
* Use Docker and containers to create reliable, repeatable development and test environments.
* Contribute to embedded Linux software and the interfaces between it and our microcontroller firmware.

**About you**

You enjoy seeing firmware come to life in real hardware, and you like being close to the bench, motors and sensors rather than hidden away from the physical system. You are comfortable owning firmware end to end, from first requirements and architecture through to code that ships, and you get energy from solving problems with people from different technical backgrounds.

* A strong track record of designing and delivering embedded systems, with the judgement to take ownership and make pragmatic technical decisions independently.
* Extensive professional experience developing firmware in C and/or C++ on ARM microcontrollers, ideally STM32.
* Strong experience developing and maintaining automated tests for embedded systems, including using them within continuous integration workflows.
* Confidence working directly with hardware and independently debugging complex systems at both code and signal level.
* Strong skills in interpreting component datasheets and electronics schematics, and using them to inform design and debugging.
* A collaborative, entrepreneurial approach, with the ability to explain technical trade-offs, support other engineers and solve problems with people from very different disciplines.

# **Principal Engineer**

## **About this role**

The bar has moved. Five years ago a strong engineer was measured by what they could build and how well they could mentor others to build it. Today, with Claude Code and agents, we produce quality work at a speed that would have looked superhuman in 2022.

What separates exceptional from good is no longer typing speed or local craftsmanship. It is the complete package: architecture, deep engineering foundations, communication, system thinking, and the judgement to direct both your own intelligence and AI toward outcomes that matter.

Exceptional people at this level are not the best implementer in the room; they are the person whose specifications, decisions, and review judgement compound into systems that work in production and that others (and agents) can build on. They are a force multiplier, they hold a room at the highest levels, and clients treat them as the SME by default.

## **Your mindset**

The mindset is the engine, and it is almost impossible to teach retrospectively. You are outcome obsessed, not output obsessed and you care whether the problem was actually solved - you resist the ego instinct to admire a clever solution and ask whether it was needed at all.

You are intellectually honest about uncertainty, taking a trust-but-verify approach and assuming the surprising bug is the one that will burn. You are deeply pragmatic, which matters at CreateFuture where pace counts: you have outgrown the religious wars about platforms, languages and patterns, you hold opinions loosely, and you decide for the systems in front of you, not the ones you wish you had.

You have a bias toward delivery: the smallest thing that works, then iterate, treating documents and meetings as means to that end.

And you are relentlessly curious beyond any immediate need, wanting to know how the database actually stores things or why a Claude Opus inference call costs what it does, which keeps you several layers ahead while the rest of the team is still reading the API docs.

## **AI as the accelerant**

For a Principal to be truly exceptional, this is now already a first-class competency in your arsenal, not a side skill.  An engineer who is brilliant by last year's standards but not fluent with AI is not exceptional in 2026. In practice that means:

* **Setting AI up to succeed.** You treat context engineering as a craft (the right files, specs, examples and constraints), and you architect systems with clean interfaces, good naming, machine-readable specs and knowledge bases so the codebase is a quality baseline AI can work on later. No separate ivory-tower architect required.
* **Reviewing and choosing well.** You read far more code than you write, and your value is in the quality of review: catching the silent assumption, the security flaw, the architectural drift, knowing where models fail and looking there first. You pick the right tool for the job (Claude Code for a deep refactor, an inline assistant when that is enough, a sub-agent for parallel work, the right model for analysis versus generation) and you know the constraints differ by client, an enterprise like PayPoint or Natwest versus a scale-up type business like Zuto or OAG.
* **Working with non-determinism.** You see where AI moves the bottleneck and help people left and right of you unblock the value stream. You build with AI components but know success is no longer a binary, reaching for evals, golden datasets, structured outputs and fallback paths as naturally as you reach for unit tests.

## **Technical breadth across the full stack**

Exceptional means depth in at least one area but competence everywhere the system reaches.

* **Backend:** an instinct for distributed systems (what fails, what is eventually consistent, where queues back up), APIs that age well, thoughtful data modelling, and an understanding that languages are mostly syntax differences you can close with AI.
* **Cloud:** cost-aware and security-aware by default, reaching for IaC, composing the primitives rather than stitching together managed services and hoping it works.
* **Data:** modern pipelines, governance and lineage, increasingly vector stores and embeddings, with data quality treated as seriously as production code because garbage in, garbage out is far worse once AI features depend on it.
* **Web and mobile:** past the framework arguments, with a clear view on what you would pick today, and able to build "good enough" front ends yourself with AI.

Full-stack here means seeing the platform as one system and knowing which levers matter most. It does not mean front-end work with a few Node.js servers.

### 

## **System thinking, consulting and commercial judgement**

At CreateFuture we work in a consultancy context, where many otherwise excellent IC engineers can struggle.

You know technology is roughly 30% of the picture; the rest is design, argument and reasoning, commercial and political acumen, and the clarity to frame outcomes for a COO, CTO, CIO or CEO in their own language.

You know when gold-plating is wasteful, you can name when a project's real problem is not technical and say so even when it is awkward, and you have a strong sense of what is durable versus what is fashion.

You are not the engineer who introduced the team to seven new technologies last year; you are the one who removed three and quietly made the remaining stack stronger.

## **Skills**

* **★ Java containerisation on codebases that were never built for it**
* **★ Developer experience — tooling, pipelines, the inner loop**
* **★ Replatform, refactor and rebuild judgment**
* CI/CD pipeline integration and non-prod smoke testing
* Reference implementations and migration factory assets
* Reading automated dependency and code analysis critically
* Mentoring senior engineers across sites

## **Leadership mentality**

Technical work is necessary but no longer sufficient. By default you raise the level of everyone around you, regardless of discipline.

* Communicate clearly and frequently (documents, decisions, post-mortems, design notes); the written artefact is the machine-readable context we can feed to AI later.
* Make decisions and own them. You don't escalate everything or hoard control, and you are willing to be the benevolent dictator when it is your turn.

# Head of Compensation & Benefits (US & EMEA)

**SHREWSBURY, UK**(Hybrid Working - 3 days in the office per week)   
  
A benchmarked salary between **£68,600 to £83,600**. Your salary level is determined by skills and experience within our progression framework.

### COMPANY OVERVIEW

---

﻿Croud is an independent global media, creative, and data agency helping our clients make their next best move. ﻿We help brands unlock growth with Return on Intelligence - applying innovative intelligence across brand strategy, integrated media, social, creative, and data. We deliver this through our proprietary tech platform, CroudOS, our Croudie network and our award-winning global teams.

Founded in 2011 to reinvent the agency model, Croud combines 600+ in-house digital experts with a global network of 2,900 on-demand marketing specialists. This unique business model﻿ enables us to operate with agility, delivering tailored solutions that drive meaningful and measurable growth for our clients in over 120 markets and 60+ languages.

Croud was recently named a Sunday Times Best Place to Work for the second year in a row, and was named Performance Marketing Employer of the Year by PMW

At Croud, we unlock potential by elevating our people, clients, and communities within a rapidly advancing and complex economy. We operate as a unique scaled network of Intelligent, Creative Specialists, enabling us to deliver superior brand outcomes and unlock potential for our people, our clients and our communities.

Our culture is strategically driven and inspired by a shared long-term vision. It is collaborative and connected, with a focus on continuous learning and mutual support.

### ROLE OVERVIEW

---

As **Head of Compensation & Benefits (US & EMEA)**, you will be the strategic lead and operational owner of our total rewards strategy, employee benefits and payroll operations across North America and EMEA.

Reporting directly to the **CPO**, you will shape and deliver a globally aligned reward framework that supports our business strategy, attracts and retains world-class talent, and enables consistent, competitive and equitable reward practices across our markets.

The role combines strategic leadership across **job architecture, market benchmarking, salary structures and incentive design** with strong operational oversight. You will have accountability for the end-to-end payroll process, including final checks and sign-off on global payroll runs, ensuring accuracy, compliance and timely delivery.

You will also lead the selection and management of reward and payroll partners, ensuring robust governance and compliance with the legal and tax requirements of the jurisdictions in which we operate. Working closely with senior stakeholders across the business, you will bring together strategy, data and operational rigour to continuously evolve our compensation and benefits offering.

### RESPONSIBILITIES

---

#### **1. Strategic Reward & Compensation Planning**

* Design, implement, and govern market-competitive salary structures, bonus schemes, and incentive programs tailored across EMEA and US markets.
* Conduct annual global salary benchmarking, equity, and market adjustments using industry data (e.g., Mercer).
* Co-lead the annual performance, bonus and compensation review cycle, partner with Finance on budget allocation, and model scenario planning.
* Oversee job architecture, grading frameworks, and role evaluation systems across diverse regions.

#### **2. Benefits Management & Provider RFP**

* Evaluate, consolidate, and manage external benefits, health, wellness, and pension providers across US (e.g., 401(k), medical options) and EMEA locations.
* Lead RFP processes and contract negotiations to streamline multi-market benefits under unified, cost-effective vendors where appropriate.
* Monitor market practices to ensure regional benefits programs are competitive, inclusive, and compliant with local tax/legal mandates.

#### **3. Payroll Governance & Operational Oversight**

* Execute final checks and formal approval on monthly/bi-weekly multi-country payroll submissions prior to release, ensuring 100% accuracy and compliance.
* Manage third-party payroll providers across US and EMEA jurisdictions, establishing strict SLAs and performance benchmarks.
* Oversee payroll operations integration, standardising workflows and reducing manual intervention.

#### **4. Compliance, Tax & Risk Mitigation**

* Maintain up-to-date knowledge of US (Federal/State) and EMEA regional employment law, statutory tax requirements, and statutory benefits mandates.
* Manage statutory reward reporting processes with help of the People Operations Team, including mandatory disclosures (e.g., Gender Pay Gap reporting where applicable).
* Lead cross-functional alignment with Legal and Finance on tax, audit readiness, and risk management.

### PERSON SPECIFICATION

---

We’re looking for an experienced **Compensation & Benefits / Total Rewards leader** who can operate confidently at both strategic and operational levels. You’ll be comfortable shaping reward strategy for a complex, international organisation while also being hands-on enough to challenge the detail, spot risk and ensure our payroll and benefits operations are delivered accurately and effectively.

#### **Experience & Expertise**

* Significant experience in **Compensation & Benefits, Total Rewards or Reward leadership**, ideally within a complex, multi-country organisation.
* Strong experience designing and implementing **global or multi-market compensation frameworks**, including salary structures, job architecture, grading and benchmarking.
* Demonstrable experience managing **US and EMEA compensation and benefits**, with a strong understanding of the differences between markets and the ability to balance global consistency with local requirements.
* Strong knowledge of **market benchmarking, pay structures, incentive and bonus design**, and the use of external market data to inform reward decisions.
* Experience leading or significantly contributing to **annual compensation, bonus and performance review cycles**, including modelling budgets and scenarios in partnership with Finance.
* Proven experience managing **employee benefits programmes and providers**, including RFPs, contract negotiations, renewals and vendor performance.
* Strong understanding of **multi-country payroll operations and governance**, including experience managing third-party payroll providers and reviewing payroll outputs for accuracy and compliance.
* Good working knowledge of **US federal/state and EMEA employment, payroll, tax and statutory benefit requirements**, with the judgement to know when specialist Legal or tax advice is required.
* Experience working with **HRIS, payroll and reward technology**, with a track record of improving processes, data quality and automation.
* Experience working with senior stakeholders, including **C-suite and executive leadership**, and the confidence to provide clear, evidence-based recommendations on complex reward matters.

#### **Skills & Capabilities**

* **Strategic thinker:** able to translate business and people strategy into practical, scalable reward programmes.
* **Commercially astute:** understands the financial implications of reward decisions and can balance competitiveness, affordability and employee value.
* **Data-driven:** confident analysing market data, modelling scenarios and using insight to inform recommendations and decisions.
* **Operationally rigorous:** highly detail-oriented, with a strong focus on accuracy, governance, controls and risk management — particularly where payroll is concerned.
* **Strong communicator:** able to explain complex compensation, benefits, payroll and compliance matters clearly to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
* **Influential partner:** builds trusted relationships with People, Finance, Legal and senior business leaders and can confidently challenge when required.
* **Problem solver:** comfortable navigating ambiguity, resolving complex issues and finding pragmatic solutions across different markets.
* **Change-oriented:** able to simplify, standardise and improve processes while recognising where local market requirements need to be retained.
* **Highly organised:** able to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, vendors and stakeholders across different countries without losing sight of the detail.
* **Discreet and trusted:** demonstrates sound judgement when handling highly confidential employee, salary and business information.

#### **What would make you stand out**

* Experience in a **high-growth, international or PE-backed organisation** where reward frameworks and processes are evolving.
* Experience bringing together or harmonising **different reward, benefits or payroll approaches following organisational change, acquisition or international expansion**.
* Experience working within a **professional services, agency, technology or similarly talent-driven environment**.
* Experience implementing or optimising **reward technology, payroll systems or HRIS integrations**.
* A track record of using **automation, data and technology** to improve the employee and People team experience while strengthening controls.
* Professional qualification or relevant accreditation in **Reward, Compensation & Benefits, HR, Payroll or a related discipline** is desirable but not essential.

#### **Our ideal person**

You’re a **strategic reward leader who is not afraid of the detail**. You can move comfortably from presenting a global compensation recommendation to the CPO, to challenging a payroll variance or negotiating with a benefits provider.

You bring **curiosity, commercial judgement and a continuous-improvement mindset**, and you’re motivated by building reward programmes that are fair, competitive, sustainable and genuinely support the way our people and business operate.

At Croud, our vision centres around the idea of unlocking potential. We do this by elevating everyone in an inclusive and progressive culture, empowering individuals to deliver their best work.
