# Senior E-commerce Backend Engineer: AI Native (f/m/d)

*York, UK*

Edmund Optics® is a leading manufacturer and supplier of optics, imaging, and photonics technology. Edmund Optics` state-of-the-art manufacturing capabilities combined with its global distribution network has earned it the position as being one of the largest supplier of off-the-shelf optical components and a trusted partner when it comes to customized solutions. Supporting numerous markets around the globe, including advanced diagnostics, semiconductor & electronics, machine vision, automation, and R&D; Edmund Optics products are used in a variety of applications ranging from DNA sequencing to retinal eye scanning to high-speed factory automation.

Edmund Optics Europe, a US owned-group consisting of Edmund Optics subsidiaries in Germany, UK, Netherlands and France, is responsible for sales, marketing, distribution, engineering and application support for a wide product range throughout Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Europe is one of the main growth markets for Edmund Optics globally, leading to a rapidly expanding and developing local team.

To accelerate our success and growth within the European Market, Edmund Optics Ltd. is looking for a

## **Senior E-commerce Backend Engineer: AI Native (f/m/d)**

  
The Senior E-commerce Backend Engineer: AI-Native is responsible to build, integrate, and expand the backend services that power the company's evolving modular e-commerce platform. This is a hands-on software engineering role focused on connecting core e-commerce capabilities including personalization, semantic and LLM-driven search and discovery, Digital Asset Management (DAM), Product Information Management (PIM), and internal SAP/HANA systems. The role will design and develop APIs, services, data flows, and integrations that allow these platforms to work together reliably at scale. A defining requirement for this position is an AI-native development mindset: the successful candidate will use AI coding agents as a normal part of the software development lifecycle to generate, refactor, test, debug, document, and improve code while applying strong engineering judgment, security practices, and human review. The ideal candidate combines strong backend engineering fundamentals, systems integration experience, curiosity, and the ability to move quickly in a modern AI-assisted development environment.  
  

### Essential Functions:

* Backend Platform Development: Design, build, maintain, and extend backend services, APIs, and integration layers that support Edmund Optics' modular e-commerce architecture and customer-facing web experiences
* AI-Native Software Development: Use AI coding agents and agentic development workflows as a core part of day-to-day engineering to generate, refactor, test, debug, document, and accelerate production code. Validate AI-generated output for correctness, security, maintainability, and performance rather than treating generated code as automatically production-ready
* E-commerce Systems Integration: Integrate key e-commerce capabilities including personalization platforms, semantic/LLM search and discovery, DAM, PIM, analytics and data services, and other modular components as the e-commerce ecosystem evolves
* Enterprise Data & ERP Integration: Build and maintain reliable integrations between the e-commerce platform and internal enterprise systems, including SAP/HANA, product, pricing, inventory, customer, order, and other business data required to support e-commerce experiences and transactions
* API & Service Architecture: Develop scalable, secure, well-documented APIs and services that allow internal applications, third-party platforms, and customer-facing experiences to exchange data efficiently and consistently
* LLM & Semantic Capabilities: Partner with e-commerce, search, data, and AI teams to integrate LLM-enabled and semantic capabilities into the site, including retrieval, product discovery, conversational experiences, and supporting data pipelines or service layers
* Quality, Testing & Debugging: Build automated testing and validation into development workflows. Use AI-assisted debugging where appropriate while maintaining strong standards for code review, observability, performance, regression prevention, and production reliability
* Modular Architecture & Reusability: Develop services and components with clear boundaries, reusable interfaces, and maintainable integration patterns that support continued movement toward a more modular and composable e-commerce architecture
* Vendor & Partner Collaboration: Work directly with technology vendors, implementation partners, and internal teams to understand technical requirements, review integration approaches, troubleshoot issues, and translate platform capabilities into production solutions
* Continuous Improvement & Emerging Tools: Stay current with AI-assisted software development, agentic coding workflows, backend architecture, integration patterns, and emerging e-commerce technologies. Evaluate new approaches pragmatically and adopt those that measurably improve engineering speed, quality, or maintainability

### Qualifications:

To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable Accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

### Your profile:

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related technical field; equivalent relevant experience will be considered
* 7+ years of professional software development experience, including substantial hands-on backend, API, or systems integration work
* Experience working with SAP and/or SAP HANA data and integration patterns
* Demonstrated recent experience using AI-assisted or agentic coding workflows in real software development, not solely experimentation or prompt-based prototyping
* Strong hands-on backend software engineering experience building production web applications, services, APIs, and integrations
* Strong engineering judgment and demonstrated ability to use AI coding agents and AI-assisted development tools to write, refactor, test, debug, and document code as part of a professional software development workflow
* Experience designing and consuming RESTful APIs, service integrations, data interfaces, and modern backend application patterns
* Experience integrating multiple enterprise or SaaS platforms within a production web or e-commerce environment
* Strong understanding of databases, data modeling, SQL, system-to-system data flows, error handling, and integration reliability
* Experience with source control, automated testing, code review, CI/CD practices, logging, monitoring, and production troubleshooting
* Ability to work effectively with frontend developers, architects, product and e-commerce teams, data teams, enterprise application owners, and external implementation partners
* Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and comfort working in an evolving environment where architecture and tools will continue to change
* Ability to communicate technical concepts, trade-offs, risks, and dependencies clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
* Fluency in English

### What we offer:

A versatile and challenging position alongside a highly competitive employment package within our dynamic and successful corporation in a growing and future-proof industry. You will have the opportunity to work with highly motivated, self-driven and open-minded people with a great team spirit.

Edmund Optics provides a range of employee benefits alongside the salary package including:

* Company pension scheme
* Private medical & dental insurance
* Extensive training and development opportunities
* Subsidized gym membership
* Cycle to Work scheme
* Company events
* ...and a lot more!

Please send your applications to hr-uk@edmundoptics.co.uk.

We are looking for someone who is ready to challenge themselves by learning new technologies, lead developer teams and understand a product from end to end.

Actively participate and own the design, development and delivery of full stack products from frontend to backend.

Strong backend development experience using Node.js, Java, Python, .NET or similar technologies.
Proven ability to design and build scalable APIs and distributed systems.
Solid experience with relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.
Experience with testing frameworks, unit testing, integration testing and automated testing strategies.
Strong understanding of software development best practices, system design, maintainability and code quality.
Experience working in agile, cross-functional teams and contributing to delivery planning and estimation.
Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure or GCP, CI/CD pipelines or DevOps practices would be beneficial.
Exposure to NoSQL databases, microservices or event-driven architectures would be desirable.

 
To qualify for the role, you must have
 

Strong technical decision-making ability.
Excellent problem-solving skills with a proactive approach to challenges.
Confident communicator, able to engage with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
A mentor mindset with a passion for developing others and raising team capability.
High level of ownership, accountability and attention to detail.

Support, coaching and feedback from some of the most engaging colleagues around
Opportunities to develop new skills and progress your career
The freedom and flexibility to handle your role in a way that’s right for you

# Founding ML Engineer — Live Music Intelligence

Gotobeat – The operating system for live music

Location: Remote-first (UTC to UTC+3 preferred) | Type: Full-time | Reports to: Head of Tech

Salary: Competitive + equity

How to apply: send your CV to alfredo@gotobeat.com

---

## The problem

Can this artist fill this room, in this city, on this Thursday? Every promoter bets their own money on that question, and most of them answer it with gut feel, a Spotify listener count and a phone call to a friend. A good answer puts the right act in a 300-cap room in Leeds two summers before it headlines a festival. A bad answer leaves a half-empty venue and a lost deposit.

We built a system that answers it better than gut feel. It is called Antonello. We are hiring the person who will own it.

## About Gotobeat

Gotobeat builds software for live music: for the artists who play, the venues that host and the promoters who book. We help emerging artists earn more, venues fill more seats and promoters spend less time on admin. The platform covers planning, promotion, ticketing and post-show settlement. It runs on an AWS serverless stack, Python data pipelines and LLM agents.

## Why this role matters

Most music data companies see one slice: streams, or social, or ticket sales. Gotobeat is a ticketing platform and a promoter tool, so we hold the dataset that ties them together: what an artist streamed, what they posted, where they played and how many people paid at the door. That join is the most valuable thing we own. Today one founder maintains it.

You are the first hire whose whole job is that data. You take over the models, the pipelines and the storage, and you own them end to end: from the notebook where a feature starts to the number a promoter reads before they sign a deal. When your forecast moves, shows get booked or not. The feedback is an empty room or a full one.

## What you take over on day one

* **Antonello, the capacity engine.** A per-city venue-capacity forecast: an XGBoost ensemble over an event-history prior, calibrated ranges, confidence gates that hold back a weak prediction, and an LLM evidence-repair loop that finds the shows our scrapers missed.
* **The discovery loop.** A daily pipeline that pulls new artists from Songstats, Spotify playlists and related-artist graphs, runs them through fit gates, genre families and liveness checks, and gives a promoter a shortlist that matches their taste and their rooms.
* **The data estate.** DynamoDB as the system of record, a change-data-capture mirror into a normalised Postgres schema on Supabase, S3 snapshots, and the API clients and data-partner integrations for streaming, social and touring data.
* **The analytics.** Sell-through and price suggestions, the hype and momentum scores, ad attribution across Meta and Google, and a rule engine that checks the model when the evidence is thin.

## What you'll do

* **35%** Build the best artist model in the music industry. Antonello forecasts what an act can draw in a city. Your job is to make that the number the industry trusts. Retrain it, recalibrate it and score it against what happened at the door. Decide when it should stay silent. Ship each improvement to production yourself.
* **25%** Own the data pipeline and the ingestion. Keep every source complete, fresh and cheap, and make the join between streaming, social, touring and ticket sales something a colleague can query in one line.
* **15%** Own the architecture of the data estate: the single-table design, the change-data-capture mirror into Postgres, and the schema every model and every query reads. Design the contracts so a new source or a new model plugs in without a migration weekend.
* **15%** Build the analytics a promoter bets on: expected sell-through, the right ticket price, which ad spend sold tickets, and the confidence behind each number.
* **10%** Expose the models as tools our LLM agents call, with the evaluation and the guardrails that let an agent draft a deal from a forecast.

## The stack

* Python 3.13 in Lambda containers for the models and the scrapers: XGBoost, numpy, Playwright.
* TypeScript on Node for the orchestration, the API and the promoter product: AWS Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SST v3 as infrastructure as code.
* DynamoDB with ElectroDB, DynamoDB Streams into Supabase Postgres, S3 for snapshots and artefacts.
* Claude, Gemini and Perplexity for the agents, called through MCP tool surfaces.
* No Kubernetes, no Spark cluster, no GPU farm. The data is small: tens of thousands of artists, hundreds of thousands of shows and the ticket sales behind them.
* No pager. The crons run overnight and the alarms land in Slack.

## You'll be successful here if you have

* Substantial experience of shipping machine learning that people relied on, including at least one model that was wrong in production and what you learned from it.
* Depth in tabular ML and forecasting: gradient boosting, calibration, evaluation on small and noisy data, and a preference for the simpler model that you can explain to a promoter.
* Data engineering: you have designed a schema, owned a pipeline end to end and made an expensive source cheap.
* Fluent Python, and enough TypeScript to ship the glue yourself.
* Practical LLM engineering: tool use, retrieval and evaluation, and a clear view of when a model must ask before it acts.
* Experience of building on your own: from a blank repo to something people use, with nobody else writing the tickets.
* A love of live music. You have stood in a half-empty room and known why.

### Nice to have

* Experience of music or entertainment data, for example at a streaming service, a data provider, a ticketing platform, a label or a booking agency.
* Experience with streaming, social or touring APIs, and with an ingestion that survives an upstream change.
* Experience with AWS serverless data patterns and change-data-capture pipelines.
* Experience with the MCP tool protocol and agent evaluation.

---

## How we work

* Remote-first, with quarterly in-person hack weeks in London.
* A small, senior team with no management layers and a lot of autonomy.
* One-week sprints, async communication and fast decisions.
* The founder who built the current models works with you for the first months, then hands over.
* We value clean code, continuous learning and doing right by artists.

## Benefits

* Competitive salary, set by experience, plus founding-team equity.
* Fully remote, with the hours that suit you.
* We engage you as an employee or as a contractor, according to the country where you live.
* Unlimited paid holiday, plus local public holidays.
* Free gig tickets and backstage passes to all Gotobeat shows.
* A budget for the hardware, the data and the conferences you need.

---

## Hiring process

1. Intro chat (30 min): the role, the music and whether we make sense to each other.
2. Technical deep dive (90 min): you walk us through a model you shipped, then we pair on a prediction from our data that went wrong. No LeetCode, no take-home.
3. Founders' chat (30 min): vision, values, equity and any remaining questions.

Total time from first call to offer: about two weeks.

---

## Ready to join Gotobeat?

Send your CV to alfredo@gotobeat.com with the subject line "Founding ML Engineer – [Your Name]". Tell us about a model you shipped and what it got wrong, and name one artist you think is about to break. We reply within five business days.

Gotobeat is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from everyone. Tell us if you need any adjustment to the process.

We use your application only to assess you for this role. We keep it for six months after the role closes, then we delete it. See the privacy policy for your rights.

## Who we are

Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards. 

As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously.

We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications. 

## The role

Helsing delivers AI-powered capabilities that redefine machine perception and decision-making. Our technology powers a range of UAS platforms, accelerating critical mission functions.  
  
You will work in a dedicated Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC) team and take full end-to-end responsibility for developing and validating state estimation, navigation and guidance algorithms. In close collaboration with field engineers, your goal is to elevate the performance of our UAS platforms to unprecedented levels and impact the future of defense technology.

## The day-to-day

* Own the development of bespoke controllers for UAS end to end; through conception, design, simulation, physical integration and feature iteration.
* Design, test and implement state estimator algorithms that work robustly in contested environments
* Simulate the performance of navigation and guidance algorithms to inform the definition of sensor stacks, which could include IMUs, GPS/GNSS, barometers, magnetometers and advanced image-based positioning systems
* Analyse real sensor and test data to calibrate sensors and validate performance, closing the simulation-to-real gap
* Support the specification and execution of tests for navigation and guidance algorithm evaluation
* Collaborate with interfacing disciplines such as Flight Mechanics, Aerodynamics, Embedded Hard- and Software, and Testing
* Contribute to, follow and analyse flight tests

## You should apply if you

* Hold a M.Sc. or PhD in Aeronautical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics or an equivalent degree
* Have at least 5 years of professional experience in navigation, guidance or state estimation development
* Have very good skills in Matlab/Simulink
* Have a solid background in state estimation theory, aerodynamics, stability and control, and systems modelling
* Have excellent communication skills and the ability to report and present findings clearly and efficiently both internally and externally
* Possess solid software engineering skills, writing clean and well-structured code in Matlab and/or languages like Python, Rust, Java, or modern C++
* Are passionate about keeping up to date with current research and enjoy reimplementing / extending papers on state of the art navigation and guidance algorithms

**Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically* *under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.**

## Nice to Have

* Hands-on experience with fixed-wing aircraft / drones
* Have worked with or even contributed to open-source autopilots like Ardupilot or PX4

## Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields

* Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns
* The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world
* Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. ## Job Description

**Location:**The role requires a minimum of three days per week office attendance**.**

The Health, Safety and Security (HSS) Director is accountable for leading the end-to end HSS function across HS2 Ltd and its supply chain. The role sets the strategic direction, defines the technical safety standards to deliver a minimum performance safety standard, and drives delivery of health, safety, and security outcomes to achieve performance beyond industry best practice. Operating at Executive level, the role ensures the organisation delivers a safe, secure, and resilient railway, embeds a strong safety culture, and meets all regulatory and Development Agreement obligations. The role also establishes the frameworks, systems, and capabilities required to manage and assure health and safety risk, performance, and respond effectively to health and safety incidents.

HS2 Ltd endeavours to ensure everyone working for us and with us feels included, thrives and achieves their full potential. In practice, this means we are positive and inclusive about making adjustments, providing flexible working, encouraging our staff networks to flourish and providing personal and professional development opportunities.

**About the role:**

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Lead HS2’s approach as an Intelligent Safety Client, setting and delivering Health, Safety and Security strategy (Safe at Heart) across HS2 Ltd and its supply chain, aligning to organisational priorities and legacy ambitions.
* Lead the HS2 approach to Health, Safety and Security, establishing clear direction, expectations, and governance and leaving a lasting legacy for health & safety across both HS2 and the industry.
* Work in partnership with Executive and Delivery Directors to achieve health and safety performance beyond industry best practice, actively intervening to correct performance.
* Champion a strong, visible safety culture (“Safe at Heart”) across all levels of the organisation.
* Champion best practice, innovation to set new standards in health and safety risk exposure, minimising long-term industry prevalent health and occupational impacts.

**Performance & Assurance**

* Establish and lead integrated frameworks for managing HSS risks across the programme.
* Accountable for overall health and safety performance across HS2 Ltd and its supply chain, defining health and safety technical standards, including Occupational Health, to drive a minimum safety performance level.
* Establish performance frameworks, tools, processes, metrics, and reporting to monitor and continuously improve outcomes.
* Deliver proactive risk assurance through data, intelligence, and insight to inform strategic priorities, assurance and auditing interventions early and mitigate safety risk exposure before it becomes a trend.

**Policy, Standards & Compliance**

* Define and maintain HSS policies, standards, and management systems.
* Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including ISO standards and Development Agreement obligations.
* Provide assurance to the Executive and Board on HSS performance and compliance.

**Risk, Safety & Security Management**

* Establish and lead integrated frameworks for managing HSS risks across the programme.
* Define and implement a robust framework for managing safety and security incidents, including response, escalation, and lessons learned.
* Lead organisational capability in incident response, crisis management, business continuity, and resilience.

**Delivery Support & Integration**

* Provide expert HSS advice to delivery teams and enable safe delivery through specialist support services.
* Ensure effective integration of HSS requirements across assets, projects, and supply chain partners.
* Embed safety, health, and security considerations throughout the full programme lifecycle.

**People & Capability**

* Lead and develop a high-performing, multi-disciplinary HSS function.
* Build capability across HS2 and its supply chain to deliver consistent HSS standards.
* Promote continuous improvement, learning, and professional development.

**Governance & Stakeholder Engagement**

* Support Executive governance and Board assurance, including relevant sub committees.
* Engage with regulators, government, JV partners, and external stakeholders to ensure alignment and compliance.

**Culture & Inclusion**

* Promote safety leadership, wellbeing, and inclusion across the organisation.
* Embed consistent behaviours, values, and expectations aligned to HS2 ways of working.

**About you:**

**Skills:**

* Strategic leadership of safety, health, and security in complex environments.
* Strong influencing and stakeholder management at Executive and system level.
* Risk-based decision-making and crisis leadership capability.
* Ability to drive cultural change and sustained performance improvement.
* Data-led thinking and performance insight application.
* Clear communication of complex regulatory and technical issues.

**Knowledge:**

* Health, safety, and security management in major infrastructure programmes.
* Regulatory frameworks and standards (e.g., HSE, ISO).
* Risk, assurance, and incident management frameworks.
* Performance management and data-driven safety approaches.
* Information security and SIRO responsibilities.

* Proven track record of improving safety performance across organisations and supply chains.

**About IonQ:**

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. We are looking for a Physicist, System Operations to join our Resilience Engineering & Operations team at IonQ. In this role you will operate, maintain and improve our trapped-ion quantum computers, contributing to the team's mission of keeping our quantum systems running reliably, safely and effectively.

You will take ownership of system maintenance and day to day operational performance, working closely with cross-functional teams to ensure our commercial and development systems remain available and well understood. This role sits at the intersection of physics, hardware operations and system reliability, and will help shape how we scale operational excellence across our quantum platforms.

Maybe you've run a YouTube channel, cut your own reels, or built a following explaining something complicated to camera. Maybe you're the associate whose training decks got passed around the whole department. You’ll sit within the legal engineering team, and own the production and currency of Legora Academy, our education platform used across the whole company: scripting, directing, coordinating recordings, and keeping a library of high-production videos current as the product evolves at AI speed. Around 30% of your time stays on live client work, weighted toward new-feature pilots and lighthouse deployments, because the best teaching material comes from real deployments, not theory. Owning Legora Academy content production end to end: writing and revising scripts, directing and coordinating recording with practice-group Legal Engineers, and keeping the video library current so nothing teaches an old version of the product.

Building the Legal Engineering enablement assets for every product launch: guides, FAQs, known limitations and demo suites, so no one is caught off guard by what ships.

Are an experienced legal engineer, or a qualified lawyer (2 to 4 PQE) with hands-on legal AI experience: able to script, build and troubleshoot use cases across a platform without supervision.

Care deeply about quality, but don’t get stuck in perfectionism: you get things done, and you make them better over time.

**Build a career as a eCommerce Project Manager - Hybrid Working - Salary DOE**

**Powered by Retail Success, magic42** has gone from strength to strength and established itself as one of Birmingham's leading eCommerce development agencies. Don't take our word for it, **check out our customer and GlassDoor reviews!**

We're a trustworthy, collaborative team of eCommerce experts, open to new ideas and always professional, whether that's with each other or with our clients. If that sounds like the kind of place you want to build a career, we'd love to hear from you.

**About the role:**

The eCommerce Project Manager role is varied and diverse, so we are keeping an open mind in terms of backgrounds and level of experience. If you are a keen problem solver, can communicate complex ideas to others and have experience and/or interest in tech and eCommerce, this role might be for you.

We've been early adopters of AI technology as a business, and we need that same mindset in you. This isn't a nice-to-have, we're looking for genuine AI users with real fluency across AI tools, people who think AI as a natural part of how they work, not just someone who's dabbled.

No two days will be the same. You'll work with clients, developers, designers and other project managers to deliver exciting eCommerce projects.

There will be a high degree of autonomy in this role, so self-organisation, accuracy, attention to detail and personal admin skills are a must.

**What you'll do:**

* Develop and manage relationships with new and existing clients, managing a portfolio of B2C/B2B eCommerce accounts and growing them by delivering real value
* Support the delivery of end-to-end web and software projects, from requirements gathering through to launch, coordinating designers, developers, clients and finance along the way
* Translate client requirements into clear functional specifications using tools like Git and Asana, test delivered work against them, and troubleshoot when things don't go to plan
* Configure and set up eCommerce platforms, themes and third party apps and extensions, and integrate with providers such as payment gateways, ERPs and logistics systems
* Get hands on and work on platform migrations, integration data mapping etc
* Continuously identify eCommerce growth opportunities for clients, building these into a backlog of work and a development roadmap
* Support the sales process, from scoping and quotations through to proof of concepts and pitching additional work
* Support magic42's own website and marketing
* Support fellow Project Managers with writing up requirements and replicating issues
* Proactively flag any suboptimal internal processes and suggest improvements
* Provide regular business reporting and insights to your Senior Client Operations Manager and clients
* Use AI tools day to day to work smarter, from speeding up research and requirements writing to solving problems faster

* You might be an Account Manager at an agency with brilliant organisational skills looking to get more hands-on and have technical interest and/or experience
* Maybe you've built and project managed websites, understand users, their intentions and how to drive conversions, and want to dive deeper into how it all works
* Perhaps you work in eCommerce at a retailer, but have worked with stakeholders, agencies and developers to deliver changes and projects
* Perhaps you've done some development or technical support, but enjoy the business facing side more

* Excellent communication skills, verbal, written and face to face, plus the ability to communicate technical problems to non-technical people
* Excellent organisational and problem-solving skills
* Great attention to detail and process driven
* Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines
* Ability to prioritise own workload and client priorities as required
* Self-motivation and commercial acumen
* Genuine AI fluency, hands-on experience with AI tools and platforms, and an AI-forward mindset, we've been early adopters of AI technology and expect the same appetite from our team

Almost everything we run internally has been built in-house: reconciliation tooling, bank API integrations, document verification, operational reporting, and our client-facing platform. Software is not a support function here. It is how the business moves faster than firms ten times its size.

‍

‍  
We build with AI tooling as standard. We are not looking for someone who can write a linked list on a whiteboard. ‍

MoonPay is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents.

**1. About the Opportunity ✍️**

MoonPay serves a broad range of business customers, from crypto-native platforms and digital-asset companies to banks, fintechs, payment providers, global employers, marketplaces, and merchants.

Enterprise Marketing focuses on organizations evaluating MoonPay as a strategic infrastructure provider. These customers often have complex operational requirements, multiple stakeholders, longer decision-making processes, and significant needs around integration, compliance, reliability, and scale.

As Enterprise Marketing Director, you’ll define how MoonPay positions itself and goes to market with these audiences across its broader portfolio of products and capabilities. This is not a marketing role for a single product or business line. You’ll create a cohesive enterprise narrative for MoonPay while developing focused strategies for the products, use cases, industries, and customer segments within it.

This is a hands-on leadership role, initially operating as an individual contributor and partnering closely with MoonPay’s central Creative, Communications, and Marketing teams. You’ll define the strategy and personally drive its execution, from positioning and campaign development to social content, product launches, sales enablement, and performance measurement.

This role is for a versatile marketer who can move easily between strategic thinking and execution. The role is a mix of Product Marketing, Content Marketing, Social Media Marketing, and Demand Gen, so an experienced swiss army knife marketer is a perfect fit who is equal parts creative and data-driven.

On any given day, you might define the narrative for a new product, write content for X or LinkedIn, brief the Creative team on an integrated campaign, build materials for a strategic prospect, shape a customer GTM launch, or analyze which programs are contributing to the pipeline.

You’ll have significant ownership over how MoonPay shows up to enterprise audiences and the opportunity to establish the foundation from which the Enterprise Marketing function can grow.

**2. What you will do**

* Build MoonPay’s Enterprise Marketing strategy from the ground up, translating business goals into a focused go-to-market plan, campaign roadmap, editorial calendar, and day-to-day execution priorities.
* Define a cohesive enterprise narrative for MoonPay across its broader portfolio while developing differentiated positioning for specific products, capabilities, use cases, industries, and customer segments.

* Operate as the marketing lead within the Product–Sales–Marketing partnership, ensuring customer insight, product strategy, and commercial priorities translate into coordinated market execution.
* Remain hands-on across the full marketing lifecycle, developing the strategy, writing the brief, creating the content, coordinating stakeholders, launching the work, and measuring its performance.
* Own the positioning and messaging across MoonPay’s payments, stablecoin, crypto, and digital-asset infrastructure, making complex products clear, differentiated, credible, and commercially compelling.
* Develop go-to-market strategies for priority audiences, including banks, fintechs, payment providers, wallets, exchanges, marketplaces, merchants, global employers, and digital-asset businesses.
* Lead go-to-market execution for new products, capabilities, integrations, markets, and strategic partnerships—from audience definition and messaging through launch, distribution, and adoption.
* Work closely with Sales and Product to identify priority segments, use cases, buyer needs, and market opportunities based on customer conversations and active deal cycles.

* Stay directly involved in priority accounts and deals, creating tailored narratives, presentations, case studies, competitive guidance, and other materials that help Sales engage and win complex enterprise customers.

* Turn insights held across Sales and Product into scalable marketing assets, including segment playbooks, buyer-specific messaging, use-case content, sales enablement, and objection-handling frameworks.

* Build integrated campaigns across content, digital, social, events, partnerships, executive engagement, and account-based marketing to generate awareness, engagement, and qualified enterprise pipeline.

* Partner with MoonPay’s award-winning in-house Creative team to conceive and lead integrated campaigns, owning the campaign strategy, audience, brief, messaging, channel plan, stakeholder alignment, and delivery.

* Give Creative clear customer and commercial context, provide decisive feedback, and ensure the final work is both creatively strong and effective against its intended objective.

* Develop and manage MoonPay’s enterprise content strategy and calendar across LinkedIn and X, personally creating posts and longer-form content for the company and its executives that build credibility with business audiences.

* Strengthen MoonPay’s voice with enterprise audiences by developing a clear, authoritative point of view on relevant product developments, customer needs, regulatory changes, and industry conversations.

* Create high-quality content across formats, including campaign copy, thought leadership, customer stories, presentations, website copy, reports, sales materials, executive content, and event programming.
* Develop joint marketing programs with customers and strategic partners, including launch plans, case studies, co-marketing campaigns, events, and social amplification.
* Build a thought-leadership platform for MoonPay, working with executives and subject-matter experts to develop original perspectives on payments, stablecoins, crypto, treasury, tokenization, and global financial infrastructure.
* Partner with Communications to ensure product launches, customer announcements, partner news, executive thought leadership, and media activity reinforce a consistent enterprise narrative.
* Coordinate with Legal, Compliance, and Risk to ensure product claims, customer stories, campaigns, and social content are accurate and appropriate for a regulated financial business.
* Own Marketing’s contribution to enterprise pipeline, product adoption, revenue, account expansion, and partner growth, working with Sales and Revenue Operations on attribution, reporting, and performance reviews.
* Use campaign data, customer feedback, product adoption, and sales insight to evaluate performance, improve execution, and prioritize future investment.
* Establish the operating processes, repeatable programs, and evidence of impact needed to scale the Enterprise Marketing function over time.

**3. About You**

* You have 7+ years of B2B marketing experience, ideally in payments, fintech, financial infrastructure, enterprise technology, or another complex and regulated category.
* You have built or scaled a marketing function, business line, or product category from an early stage and are comfortable creating the strategy, operating model, and foundational assets yourself.
* You are a hands-on builder who is as comfortable writing a LinkedIn post, campaign brief, or sales presentation as you are defining a long-term go-to-market strategy.
* You have worked within a closely integrated Product–Sales–Marketing model and know how to turn customer conversations, product priorities, and active deals into effective marketing.
* You can create a unified portfolio narrative while developing sufficiently differentiated positioning for distinct products, customer segments, industries, and use cases.

* You have experience developing positioning and messaging for technical, API-based, platform, infrastructure, or multi-product offerings.
* You understand complex enterprise sales motions, including strategic accounts, long buying cycles, technical integrations, procurement processes, and multi-stakeholder buying committees.
* You are an exceptional writer and editor who can create sharp, credible content across X, LinkedIn, websites, campaigns, thought leadership, customer stories, executive communications, and sales materials.
* You know how to build a distinctive social voice for a B2B brand and can respond quickly to relevant industry conversations without compromising accuracy or quality.
* You have led integrated campaigns in close partnership with Creative teams, from audience insight and initial concept through briefing, production, launch, distribution, and measurement.
* You give clear creative direction, provide decisive feedback, and know how to protect a strong idea while ensuring the work serves a commercial objective.

* You have launched new products, capabilities, partnerships, or markets and understand how to coordinate Product, Sales, Creative, Communications, Legal, and other stakeholders around a shared plan.
* You are commercially minded and fluent in pipeline, account engagement, product adoption, sales velocity, win rates, expansion, attribution, and marketing ROI.
* You can balance the needs of near-term deals and launches with the longer-term work required to build market authority, brand recognition, and sustained demand.

* You are energized by creating something from the ground up and do not need a large team or established playbook to make progress.
* You operate with urgency and ownership, follow through without needing to be chased, and maintain a high standard across multiple concurrent workstreams.
* You communicate with clarity and confidence and can build trust with senior leaders, technical experts, sales teams, customers, partners and creative teams.

* You have a strong working understanding of enterprise payments, fintech, digital assets, and the broader financial-infrastructure landscape.
* Experience marketing stablecoins, on/off-ramps, treasury infrastructure, tokenization, crypto trading infrastructure, or embedded financial products is a strong plus.

# 2027 UK Graduate Programme (London & Belfast)

Oxford Economics is the world's foremost independent economic advisory firm. We enable intelligent and responsible decision-making through the provision of timely, data-driven economic and business insights and solutions our clients trust.

Our economists are experts at applying innovative economic models and research tools to provide valuable insights into essential business, financial, and policy issues. As a fast-growing, independent consultancy with a global reach, our goals are to provide outstanding analysis, forecasting and analytical tools for our clients, and challenging and rewarding careers for our staff.

# **The Programme**

We have an opportunity for exceptional economics graduates to join our teams in London and Belfast. This two-year scheme places successful candidates in six-month rotations, with opportunities across our teams including: Macro Forecasting & Analysis, Global Industry, Scenarios & Macro Modelling, Macro Consulting, Economic Footprint & Sustainability, and Tourism Economics. The rotating nature of this program, coupled with comprehensive on-the-job training, will allow you to gain in-depth practical knowledge and professional experience related to your academic and extracurricular background.

# **The Role**

As a Assistant Economist, you will be working closely with experienced economists and will be expected to take responsibility for your work from an early stage. You will contribute to Oxford Economics’ services by working with our large global team of economists on a variety of projects, including forecasting, policy analysis and bespoke economic impact modelling.

As you rotate between teams, you will have the opportunity to work on Oxford Economics’ global macro, city and sectoral forecasts and prepare articles on topical economic issues; develop econometric forecasting tools; undertake ‘what if’ scenario analysis; or assist senior economists on a variety of consultancy projects.

By the end of the programme, you will be able to:

* Apply your formal economics training to real world issues
* Interact confidently with clients and the media to explain your work
* Manage your time efficiently and balance several competing priorities
* Apply a range of analytical techniques and software packages to bring insight
* Write concisely and with impact on complex issues

# **The Teams**

During your two years in the rotation programme, you will work in four of the following teams. Please rank your top three choices in your covering letter and we will take these preferences into account when processing your application.  
  
**Macro Forecasting and Analysis (London)**

Using the Oxford Economics Global Economic Model, the macro forecasting and analysis team produces forecasts for GDP, inflation, interest rates and hundreds of other indicators for more than 200 countries updated twice a month. The team also produces written analysis on the implications of the latest economic data and policy news, and in-depth research on the critical issues that will shape the performance of economies and financial markets.  
  
**Global Industry (London)**

Our global industry team provides historical and forecast data on production, investment and profit trends at a granular level for over 100 sectors in 77 countries to inform our clients’ business planning.  It also undertakes detailed bespoke forecasting on prospects and risks to clients’ own product sales and input costs.  
  
**Scenarios and Maro Modelling (London)**

Our clients need to understand the implications of the major risks to the world economy for their businesses, whether from rapidly rising inflation, geopolitical events or climate change. Our Global Economic Model is the ideal tool for quantifying the impact of these risks, both for our Global Scenarios and Climate Services, and on a bespoke basis (e.g., for stress tests required by banks). Our macro scenarios and consulting team also undertakes research to position our clients as thought leaders on topical issues.  
 **Macro Consulting (Belfast)**Our Macro Consulting team works with clients around the world to answer complex economic and business questions using quantitative analysis, economic modelling and forecasting. The team develops bespoke models and scenarios, forecasts markets and key economic indicators, and evaluates the potential impact of economic, policy and industry developments. Projects span a wide range of sectors and geographies, helping businesses, governments and other organisations understand economic trends, assess risks and make informed strategic decisions.

**Economic Footprint (London)**

We show the social, environmental, and economic impact of our clients’ activities and help communicate these to key stakeholders. Our work ranges from in-depth modelling and quantification of the effects of economic policy changes for governments to detailed quantification of the footprint of companies on particular communities.  
  
**Tourism Economics (London and Belfast)**

Tourism Economics is an Oxford Economics company dedicated to forecasting and analytical consulting in the tourism sector. We combine an understanding of the travel sector with proven economic tools to answer the most important questions facing our clients. Our work ranges from tracking, modelling and forecasting travel sector performance, to quantifying the economic impact of visitors, events and destination marketing, to conducting policy and market analysis and bespoke research. We provide quarterly updated global forecasts to clients which cover 185 countries and over 300 cities, consistent with the economic outlook for origins and destinations.

## Training Opportunities

Graduate Economists will have the opportunity to partake in a diverse range of training opportunities, including formal training sessions designed to support you in reaching your professional and personal development goals. You will be supported by comprehensive training on the unique technical and business skills needed to handle economics projects, forecasts, and research.

Other training helps you to hone your communication, project management, presentation, and advanced econometric and Excel skills. This training will be delivered via short courses, on-the-job training, and a group project.

Your first few weeks at Oxford Economics will include a carefully curated schedule of training with leading economists, HR professionals, marketing, and program alumni.  You will learn more about the work of all of the teams across Oxford Economics and get practical training on topics such as:

* Using the Oxford Economics Global Economic Model
* Haver, Power BI and Tableau
* Econometrics applications
* Data tools
* Writing skills

## The Working Environment

Although a large global organisation with more than 700 staff in total, we strive to retain the best features of our original start-up environment. We cultivate entrepreneurial thinking by supporting staff to pursue opportunities and map their own career paths. This means an informal but hard-working culture. We offer a hybrid working model for our graduates, with three days in the office and two days from home.

With more than 20 offices around the world, you will have the opportunity to explore your interests on a global scale. As well as working hard, we encourage employees to volunteer in the community. There are regular social events and staff parties, and more informal lunchtime and evening activities, often organised by individuals.

## Requirements

Oxford Economics’ graduate employment program is for high-achieving candidates with a passion for economics who want to apply their understanding of economics to real world issues. You must be able to put together logical economic arguments and explain them convincingly to economists and non-economists alike. You will need to be a fast learner with strong analytical skills and keen attention to detail. You should be comfortable meeting tight deadlines and working under your own initiative.

Successful candidates are highly numerate and have excellent technical skills. They work well with others, take responsibility for the quality and timeliness of their work, and demonstrate a creative approach to problem-solving. The ability to communicate clearly and concisely is essential, as is fluency in English.

We welcome applications from those who meet the following requirements:

* A degree in economics or a closely related subject.
* An excellent academic record.
* Fluent English, both written and spoken.
* A demonstrable interest in economics.
* Some work experience, whether paid or voluntary (not required, but highly desirable).
* The right to work in the UK without visa sponsorship.
* We also consider applications from recent graduates with experience in academic research, the civil service, financial services, or consultancy.

# **How To Apply**

**Please submit a CV and covering letter in the application window.**In your covering letter please:  
1) list the three teams you would prefer to complete rotations with during the programme, and   
2) whether you would like to be based in London or Belfast.

We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, colour, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by the law.*

# 2027 UK Placement Programme (London, Belfast & Oxford)

Oxford Economics is the world's foremost independent economic advisory firm. We have a fantastic opportunity for hard-working economics / finance students to join our team in the United Kingdom on a one year industrial placement. Positions are available on the following teams: Macro Forecasting & Analysis, Cities & Regions, Global Industry, Scenarios & Macro Modelling, Data Team, Macro Consulting, Economic Impact, Economic Footprint & Sustainability, Tourism Economics, and Transport / Construction.

# **The Programme**

We have an opportunity for successful candidates to gain experience within areas related to their degree subject. Our students will work closely with our experienced team of economists and take on some responsibility for analysis, country forecasting and econometrics. By joining our teams, you will achieve an in-depth practical knowledge related to your degree subject.

# **The Role**

Placement positions are available in the following areas of the business:

## Macro Forecasting & Analysis (London)

Using the Oxford Economics Global Economic Model, the Macro Forecasting & Analysis team produces forecasts for GDP, inflation, interest rates and hundreds of other indicators for more than 200 countries, updated twice a month. The team also produces written analysis on the implications of the latest economic data and policy news, alongside in-depth research on the critical issues that will shape the performance of economies and financial markets.

Positions are available within the Macro Strategy and Emerging Markets, Real Estate, and Eurozone teams, situated in our award-winning Macro and Investor Services division. You should have a particular interest in macroeconomics, quantitative analysis and financial markets.

## Cities & Regions (London & Belfast)

National-level economic analysis provides only a partial guide to the dynamics unfolding in the world’s major urban centres. Our unique suite of forecasting services covers over 8,000 cities and regions across the world, providing regularly updated data, forecasts and analysis for each location. Our city consultants also work in the areas of urban and regional development, bespoke model building and location benchmarking.

As a placement student in the Cities & Regions team, you will assist in producing these regional forecasts, as well as supporting our economists in developing the quality of our services. This could include contributing to written reports or exploring novel approaches to data estimation, such as using satellite imagery to estimate regional activity. Over the course of the year, students will gain a deeper understanding of regional economics and how city performance differs from the macroeconomy, developing technical skills across the MS Office suite, EViews and the mapping software QGIS in the process.

## Global Industry (London)

Our team comprises economists who are each focused on a particular sector, such as energy generation and renewables, across the countries that we cover.

The role of the placement student is to provide support to the economists, forecast their own industries and contribute to monthly and quarterly reports. As the year progresses, placement students are given more responsibility, including forecasting some smaller macroeconomic countries, while continuing to support economists with detailed analytical work. The placement student is assigned a sector to forecast each quarter and contributes write-ups on their sector to our monthly and quarterly publications.

Our commodities team is also supported on a monthly basis by the placement student. The Industry team is involved in a number of regular and bespoke consultancy projects for large industrial firms and trade associations, and placement students typically assist with report writing and analysis. Previous placement students have made significant contributions to our flagship Global Construction reports and have been cited within publications, while others have written front-page pieces for our monthly reports.

## Scenarios & Macro Modelling (London)

Our Scenarios & Macro Modelling team focuses on designing scenarios and building macroeconomic models that help clients assess the impact of major global risks, from inflation and geopolitical tensions to climate change. Using Oxford Economics’ Global Economic Model, the team supports our Global Scenarios and Climate Services while also delivering bespoke projects such as bank stress tests. This work blends economic insight with technical modelling to provide clients with robust, data-driven answers.

As a placement student in the Scenarios & Macro Modelling team, you will gain broad exposure to economic consulting and modelling work. Most of the team’s projects involve working with the Oxford Economics Global Economic Model (GEM), one of the world’s leading large-scale commercial macroeconomic models, to develop bespoke scenarios.

You will be given more responsibility as you develop your skills and knowledge. By the end of the year, students will typically be able to support the production of macroeconomic scenarios. Scenarios are an important tool in helping clients understand the potential economic impacts of real-world events, giving you the opportunity to develop your knowledge and application of economics to real-world questions.

## Macro Consulting (Belfast)

Our Belfast team specialises in applied macroeconomic consulting and research, helping clients navigate uncertainty and make strategic decisions. Alongside tailored scenario projects, the team produces thought-leadership analysis on topical global issues, positioning clients at the forefront of industry and policy debates. This work combines strong economic expertise with the ability to communicate insights clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

The team’s placement student will assist with the production of research, taking more responsibility as the year progresses. Research topics which placement students have contributed to or led on in the past have included producing cross-country indicators of financial conditions, assessing countries’ fiscal positions post-COVID, and analysing the impact of the Russian invasion of Ukraine on countries’ terms of trade. Students also have the chance to produce country economic forecasts and write associated reports, alongside responsibilities in recurring weekly and monthly projects.

## Economic Impact (London)

We show the social, environmental and economic impact of our clients’ activities and help communicate these findings to key stakeholders. Our work ranges from in-depth modelling and quantification of the effects of economic policy changes for governments to detailed assessments of the economic footprint of companies within particular communities.

As part of this role, you will have the opportunity to assist team members across a wide range of projects. The tasks undertaken will vary according to the nature of each project and may include economic research, data analysis, modelling and contributing to client reports.

## Economic Footprint (London)

Our London-based Economic Footprint & Sustainability team supports clients in addressing the economic and policy challenges of climate change and the transition to net zero. The team applies Oxford Economics’ modelling tools and sector expertise to assess the costs, opportunities and wider implications of sustainability policies, environmental regulation and decarbonisation strategies. Their work helps businesses, governments and financial institutions understand the economic trade-offs of climate action and develop evidence-based strategies for a sustainable future.

In this role, you will support team members across various projects, with your responsibilities adapting to the specific requirements of each project. This may include data analysis, economic research, modelling and contributing to client-facing reports and presentations.

## Tourism Economics (London & Belfast)

Tourism Economics is an Oxford Economics company dedicated to forecasting and analytical consulting in the tourism sector. We combine an understanding of the travel sector with proven economic tools to answer the most important questions facing our clients. Our work ranges from tracking, modelling and forecasting travel-sector performance, to quantifying the economic impact of visitors, events and destination marketing, to conducting policy and market analysis and bespoke research. We provide quarterly updated global forecasts to clients covering 185 countries and over 300 cities, consistent with the economic outlook for origins and destinations.

This position offers the chance to collaborate with the wider team on diverse projects, with tasks changing depending on each project’s scope and objectives. Placement students may contribute to forecasting, research, data analysis and consulting work across tourism markets and destinations.

## Transport / Construction (London)

Our Transport and Construction team provides economic analysis, forecasting and advisory support across the transport, infrastructure and construction sectors. The team combines detailed sector knowledge with Oxford Economics’ economic forecasts and modelling capabilities to help clients understand market demand, assess investment opportunities and risks, and evaluate the outlook for major infrastructure and construction projects. Our work covers areas including transport infrastructure, residential and non-residential construction, engineering activity, market capacity and the economic drivers shaping future demand.

As a placement student, you will support economists across a range of forecasting, research and consulting projects. This may include analysing economic and industry data, contributing to forecasts and reports, researching market developments and assisting with bespoke client work. Over the course of the year, you will gain greater responsibility and practical experience applying economic analysis to real-world questions across the transport and construction sectors.

## Data Team (Oxford)

Our Oxford-based Data team supports the development, management and delivery of the economic data that underpins Oxford Economics’ forecasting, research and client services. The team works with large and complex datasets, helping to ensure that economic information is accurate, consistent and accessible across our models, products and analytical tools. The work combines economic understanding with data analysis and technology, including the use of programming and data-management techniques to improve processes and support the delivery of high-quality economic insight.

As a placement student, you will work alongside the team on a range of data-focused projects, supporting the collection, processing, validation and analysis of economic datasets. You will have the opportunity to develop practical experience working with large datasets and analytical tools, while building your understanding of how economic data is used across forecasting, modelling and research at Oxford Economics. Experience with tools such as Excel, R, Python, Stata or EViews would be particularly relevant to the role.

## Training Opportunities

Placement Students will have the opportunity to partake in a diverse range of training opportunities, including formal training sessions designed to support you in reaching your professional and personal development goals. You will be supported by comprehensive training on the unique technical and business skills needed to handle economics projects, forecasts, and research.

Other training helps you to hone your communication, project management, presentation, and advanced econometric and Excel skills. This training will be delivered via short courses, on-the-job training, and a group project.

Your first few weeks at Oxford Economics will include a carefully curated schedule of training with leading economists, HR professionals, marketing, and program alumni.  You will learn more about the work of all of the teams across Oxford Economics and get practical training on topics such as:

* Using the Oxford Economics Global Economic Model
* Haver, Power BI and Tableau
* Econometrics applications
* Data tools
* Writing skills

## The Working Environment

Although a large global organisation with more than 700 staff in total, we strive to retain the best features of our original start-up environment. We cultivate entrepreneurial thinking by supporting staff to pursue opportunities and map their own career paths. This means an informal but hard-working culture. We offer a hybrid working model for our graduates, with three days in the office and two days from home.

With more than 20 offices around the world, you will have the opportunity to explore your interests on a global scale. As well as working hard, we encourage employees to volunteer in the community. There are regular social events and staff parties, and more informal lunchtime and evening activities, often organised by individuals.

## Requirements

Oxford Economics’ Industrial Placement program is for high-achieving University students with studying economics who want to apply their understanding of economics to real world issues. You must be able to put together logical economic arguments and explain them convincingly to economists and non-economists alike. You will need to be a fast learner with strong analytical skills and keen attention to detail. You should be comfortable meeting tight deadlines and working under your own initiative.

Successful candidates are highly numerate and have excellent technical skills. They work well with others, take responsibility for the quality and timeliness of their work, and demonstrate a creative approach to problem-solving. The ability to communicate clearly and concisely is essential, as is fluency in English.

We welcome applications from those who meet the following requirements:

* able to undertake a 1-year industrial placement year working full time.
* a good grasp of economic theory .
* expected grade of 2:1 or above.
* experience with economic data and analysis and coursework.
* excellent written and verbal communication.
* a good eye for detail.
* proactive problem-solving approach.
* strong knowledge of Excel.

  Access/Stata/Eviews/R/Python would be a plus.

macOS Software Engineer / Senior macOS Software Engineer
 
Shape the Future of Scientific Discovery with Imaris
 
At Oxford Instruments Andor, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible in scientific imaging. As a global leader in high-performance light measuring solutions, we combine cutting-edge developments in sensors, electronics, optics and software to create technology that enables some of the world's most important scientific breakthroughs.
 
Our low-light imaging cameras, spectroscopy solutions and microscopy systems help researchers develop cancer treatments, explore the depths of space, and advance clean energy innovations. We are experts in measuring light down to a single photon and capturing events occurring within one billionth of a second.
 
The Opportunity
 
We are seeking an experienced macOS Software Engineer to take ownership of the macOS architecture for our Imaris.
 
This is a highly technical role where you'll ensure our sophisticated C++ image analysis and 3D rendering applications perform seamlessly across Apple's hardware ecosystem. You'll drive performance, reliability and scalability while maintaining cross-platform compatibility and leveraging the latest macOS technologies.
 
You'll work alongside talented Imaris software engineers, scientists and product teams to deliver innovative solutions that directly enable world-leading research and discovery.
 
What You Will Do
 
As our macOS Software Engineer, you will:

Architect, design, develop and maintain native macOS application features and cross-platform C++ core libraries.
Lead the development and optimisation of software for Apple Silicon and the wider macOS ecosystem.
Resolve complex platform-specific challenges involving rendering, memory management and multi-threading.
Deliver robust, scalable and maintainable solutions to technically demanding problems.
Drive continuous improvement across software development, testing and deployment processes.
Manage and optimise Xcode builds, CMake configurations and macOS CI/CD pipelines.
Gather requirements and contribute to the development of both new and legacy products.
Support internal teams and external customers with Mac-specific deployments and technical issues.
Participate in technical investigations, innovation initiatives and architectural decisions.
Collaborate effectively within Agile development teams.
Occasionally travel to other Andor offices and customer sites when required.

 
What We Are Looking For
Essential

Degree in Software Engineering, Physics, Computer Science or related discipline (or equivalent experience).
Minimum 5 years' experience in a software development role.
Strong proficiency in C++ and object-oriented software design.
Deep understanding of the macOS ecosystem, Apple Silicon architecture, Xcode, build pipelines and memory profiling tools.
Strong experience with Git, source control systems and collaborative development practices.
Experience across the full software development lifecycle, from requirements gathering through testing and support.
Strong knowledge of software architecture, design patterns and Clean Code principles.
Excellent understanding of data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Knowledge of Agile software development methodologies.
Proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative and solve complex technical problems.

Desirable

Experience with cross-platform UI frameworks such as Qt.
Experience transitioning and supporting cross-platform applications on macOS.
Knowledge of computer vision, image analysis or scientific imaging applications.
Experience within Life Sciences, scientific software or related domains.
Awareness of cybersecurity principles and secure software development practices.

 
About You
You will thrive in this role if you:

Enjoy solving challenging technical problems and working at a deep system level.
Take ownership and accountability for delivering results.
Balance strategic thinking with hands-on technical execution.
Communicate effectively and influence technical decisions.
Adapt quickly when priorities change.
Collaborate openly and support colleagues across teams.
Challenge existing approaches and actively contribute to continuous improvement.
Have a passion for quality, innovation and engineering excellence.

 
We Value Potential, we know that no candidate will meet every requirement listed. If you're excited by the opportunity and believe your skills, experience and passion could make an impact, we'd love to hear from you. We welcome applications from individuals whose experience may not align perfectly with every criterion.

 This permanent position is based at our headquarters in Belfast or remotely within the UK.  Please note that Oxford Instruments Andor is unable to provide visa sponsorship for these roles. Applicants must have the right to live and work in the UK at the time of application.
 
Why Join Andor & Imaris?
 
This is an opportunity to work on software that has a real-world impact. Every day, researchers around the world rely on Andor technology to make discoveries that change lives and expand human knowledge.
In return, you'll enjoy:

Meaningful work supporting world-leading scientific research
The opportunity to influence the architecture of complex, high-performance software products
Flexible remote working within the UK

Career development within Andor and the wider Oxford Instruments Group

Apply today and help us enable the next generation of scientific discovery.

# Senior Manager, Market Development, EMEAI Human Disease

OXFORDSHIRE, United Kingdom

and 2 more

## Job Description

Oxford Nanopore has developed a new generation of nanopore-based sensing technology for faster, information-rich, accessible and affordable molecular analysis, used to understand and characterise the biology of humans and diseases such as cancer. By enabling biological insights, we strive to improve life on Earth and beyond.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Market Development EMEAI – Human Disease to join our growing commercial team. In this role, the successful candidate will be responsible for driving commercial growth by expanding the total addressable Human Disease market for Oxford Nanopore Technologies across the EMEAI region. The individual for this role can be based in the UK, France or Germany. Please note that this role involves frequent travel across EMEAI, minimum 50%.

**The Details...**

This role focuses on identifying and unlocking new customer segments, applications, and geographies, translating ONT’s unique sequencing capabilities into scalable, commercially impactful market opportunities. Working at the intersection of science, policy, and commercial strategy, this role partners closely with sales, marketing, product, medical, regulatory, and government affairs teams to accelerate adoption and long‐term revenue growth.

This role has a primary focus on high-value applications in Human Disease and where Oxford Nanopore Technologies offers clear differentiation.  The role will identify and validate priority market opportunities, develop strategic partnerships and evidence-generation programs, and support the progression of promising applications from research-stage use through operationalization and production-scale deployment.

This role is suited to a highly self‐directed builder who thrives in ambiguous environments and can create momentum ahead of fully scaled organizational infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities and Duties:

Market Expansion & Growth

* Identify, assess, and validate new market opportunities for ONT technologies across research, applied, and clinical customer segments.
* Develop and execute commercial‐forward market development strategies with clear milestones and measurable growth outcomes.
* Expand market access by enabling entry into new customer segments and geographies across EMEAI.
* Provide structured input into future product, workflow, and portfolio roadmaps based on market needs and evidence gaps.

Partnerships, KOL & Ecosystem Development

* Develop strategic partnerships and collaborations to enable entry across Human Disease, including new applications.
* Build, engage, and develop Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and influencer networks aligned to ONT growth priorities.
* Lead community advocacy, education, and awareness initiatives to support market creation and adoption.
* Partner with academic, clinical, industry, and government stakeholders to strengthen ONT’s ecosystem presence.

Evidence Generation & Standards Shaping

* Define and execute evidence generation strategies, including gap analysis to support market entry for Human Disease.
